sentences.en: As the enemy raced up the slope, Harold Hardrada tightened his grip on his sword hilt and whispered one last prayer.
sentences.zh: 当敌军冲上山坡时，哈罗德·哈德拉达紧紧握住剑柄，作了最后一次祈祷。

sentences.en: There was nothing for it now, he thought, but to die with honour.
sentences.zh: 他想，现在别无他法，唯有荣誉战死。

sentences.en: He had formed his men into a tight circle, linking their shields around the raven banner, where he and Tostig stood with his friends and captains.
sentences.zh: 他把手下排成一个紧密的圆阵，将盾牌连在渡鸦战旗周围，他和托斯蒂格以及他的朋友、队长们就站在那里。

sentences.en: The Saxons, Harold thought, would have to cut their way through the line.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德心想，萨克逊人必须杀出一条血路才能突破防线。

sentences.en: He would make them pay in blood before the day was out.
sentences.zh: 他要在天黑前让对方付出血的代价。

sentences.en: The enemy was screaming out their war songs.
sentences.zh: 敌军正高声叫喊着他们的战歌。

sentences.en: Through the dust and chaos he could see Harold Godwinson at the foot of the slope, urging his men on.
sentences.zh: 透过尘土与混乱，他能看到哈罗德·戈德温森在山坡脚下催促着手下。

sentences.en: The circle was shrinking.
sentences.zh: 圆阵正在缩小。

sentences.en: Harold's men were tiring, their shield arms heavy, their sword blows weary.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德的手下们开始疲惫，举盾的手臂沉重，挥剑的动作迟缓。

sentences.en: And still the Saxons came on, eager to finish it.
sentences.zh: 而萨克逊人依然步步逼近，急于了结这一切。

sentences.en: For just a moment, Harold thought of that morning by the stream, when he was little, when Olaf had asked him what he most wanted in life.
sentences.zh: 就在那么一瞬间，哈罗德想起了溪流边的那天早晨，那时他还小，奥拉夫曾问他此生最想要什么。

sentences.en: Housecalls!
sentences.zh: 出诊！

sentences.en: So many housecalls that they would eat all half-dance cows at a single feast!
sentences.zh: 多得能在单一的一场宴会上吃光所有半舞牛的出诊！

sentences.en: What he wouldn't give for more housecalls now!
sentences.zh: 现在他愿意付出一切来换取更多出诊！

sentences.en: So there, Dominic, the epic tones of Snorri Sturluson, the 13th century historian and poet from Iceland,
sentences.zh: 就是这样，多米尼克，这是冰岛13世纪历史学家兼诗人斯诺里·斯蒂德松的史诗般语调，

sentences.en: one of the greatest writers in medieval history, whose epic account, the saga of King Harold,
sentences.zh: 他是中世纪历史上最伟大的作家之一，其史诗般的叙述《哈罗德国王萨迦》，

sentences.en: is the definitive, in fact, pretty much the only account we have of the Battle of Stamford Bridge.
sentences.zh: 是关于斯坦福桥战役最具权威的，实际上几乎是我们仅有的记载。

sentences.en: And since today's episode is about the Battle of Stamford Bridge, I mean, what else could we possibly have begun with but that great work by Snorri Sturluson?
sentences.zh: 既然今天的节目是关于斯坦福桥战役的，我的意思是，除了斯诺里·斯蒂德松那部伟大的著作，我们还能从什么开始呢？

sentences.en: I mean, really, the only choice, except perhaps for a new version, a new account of the Battle of Stamford Bridge, because actually that wasn't by Snorri Sturluson at all, was it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的，别无选择，或许除了一个新版本、对斯坦福桥战役的新记述之外，因为实际上那根本不是斯诺里·斯蒂德松写的，对吧？

sentences.en: It was by you!
sentences.zh: 那是你写的！

sentences.en: It was, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实是，没错。

sentences.en: It's a forensic reconstruction, I think it's fair to say, of what happened at that battle in Adventures in Time, Fury of the Vikings.
sentences.zh: 我想可以公正地说，这是对《时间历险：维京人之怒》中那场战役经过的法医式重建。

sentences.en: So that is literally exactly what Harold Hardrada thought.
sentences.zh: 所以这字面意思上正是哈罗德·哈德拉达当时的想法。

sentences.en: He thought back to that moment when he was a little boy, which listeners will remember from the Harold Hardrada series,
sentences.zh: 他回想起了那个还是小男孩时的时刻，听众们会在哈罗德·哈德拉达系列中记起这一点，

sentences.en: and, you know, the enemy was singing their war songs, and he could see Harold Godwinson coming on, and that's exactly what happened, Tom.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，敌人在唱着他们的战歌，他能看到哈罗德·戈德温森逼近，汤姆，事情就是这样的。

sentences.en: Because, do you know, Dominic, when we're going to go on and do the Battle of Hastings, and initially I put a passage from Millennium, my book about,
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，多米尼克，当我们接下来要讲黑斯廷斯战役时，起初我把我关于……的一本书《千禧年》中的一段放在前面，

sentences.en: which includes an account of the Battle of Hastings in the front, and then I thought, no, I shouldn't do that.
sentences.zh: 其中包含了黑斯廷斯战役的记述，然后我想，不，我不应该那样做。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there are so many other epic accounts that were written at the time, I put them in.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道的，当时写下的史诗级记述有那么多，我把它们放进去了。

sentences.en: And I did think, I wonder whether Dominic will include his account in preference to that of Snorri Sturluson, the great writer.
sentences.zh: 我确实在想，不知道多米尼克会不会把自己的记述放在伟大作家斯诺里·斯蒂德松的记述之上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you sent me the text, and you had done, and I salute you.
sentences.zh: 然后你把文本发给了我，你也确实这么做了，我向你致敬。

sentences.en: This speaks to your fundamental lack of self-confidence, I think, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这说明你骨子里缺乏自信。

sentences.en: I think that is probably what it does, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概正是它所说明的，是的。

sentences.en: Whereas I'm not burdened by the same doubts and anxieties.
sentences.zh: 而我则没有同样的怀疑和焦虑的负担。

sentences.en: No, you have the spirit of a Viking.
sentences.zh: 不，你有着维京人的精神。

sentences.en: I have the spirit of a cringing monk.
sentences.zh: 我有着唯唯诺诺修士的精神。

sentences.en: I think there is, I mean, I don't think there's any doubt about that.
sentences.zh: 我想确实有，我是说，对此毫无疑问。

sentences.en: By the way, please clip that and use that as a social media.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，请把它剪辑下来并当作社交媒体素材使用。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, I mean, today looking at one of the most exciting stories in all of medieval history,
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，我是说，今天我们要看中世纪历史上最激动人心的故事之一，

sentences.en: and it's really the last great battle between Anglo-Saxons and Vikings for the throne of England.
sentences.zh: 这确实是盎格鲁-萨克逊人与维京人为争夺英格兰王位而进行的最后一场大战。

sentences.en: And I guess this is the battle with which so many accounts of the story of the Vikings finishes, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想这也是许多维京人故事所结束的战役，对吧？

sentences.en: In almost every general English-language history of the Vikings, this is the last chapter.
sentences.zh: 在几乎所有关于维京人的通俗英语历史书中，这都是最后一章。

sentences.en: There may be a sort of epilogue, an envoi, farewell to the Viking age, but this is the last great narrative set piece.
sentences.zh: 可能有一种类似后记、送别诗的东西，向维京时代告别，但这确实是最后一个宏大的叙事高潮。

sentences.en: And you can see why, because although there are, as we'll discuss, there are subsequent attempts by Scandinavians to raid or indeed invade England.
sentences.zh: 你能明白为什么，因为尽管正如我们将要讨论的那样，斯堪的纳维亚人后来还有过突袭甚至入侵英格兰的企图。

sentences.en: This is the last great one.
sentences.zh: 但这是最后一次伟大的尝试。

sentences.en: It's the one that comes closest, and it has, it really does have the quality of myth, because at its heart are two irresistible, colourful, doomed characters,
sentences.zh: 它是最接近成功的一次，并且它确实具有神话般的品质，因为它的核心是两个势不可挡、色彩鲜明、注定走向毁灭的人物，

sentences.en: Harold Hardrada and Harold Godwinson.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·哈德拉达和哈罗德·戈德温森。

sentences.en: And both of them stand for things greater than themselves, i.e. a civilisation,
sentences.zh: 他们俩都代表着比自身更宏大的事物，即一种文明，

sentences.en: Anglo-Saxon England, as you put it, what, mead halls and moustaches?
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-萨克逊时期的英格兰，正如你所说，什么，蜜酒大厅和小胡子？

sentences.en: Yeah, and the Vikings, dragon ships and booming laughs.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有维京人，龙船和爽朗的笑声。

sentences.en: And booming laughs, exactly.
sentences.zh: 还有爽朗的笑声，完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, let us start with the man at the centre of the story, Harold Hardrada, who we talked about last week.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从故事中心的那个人开始，哈罗德·哈德拉达，我们上周谈过他。

sentences.en: So, last week we left him as King of Norway.
sentences.zh: 所以，上周我们讲到他时，他已经是挪威国王了。

sentences.en: The beginning of 1066, he's probably 50 years old.
sentences.zh: 1066年伊始，他大概50岁了。

sentences.en: So, he's the oldest of the contenders in this story.
sentences.zh: 因此，他是这个故事中年纪最大的争夺者。

sentences.en: He's had the most extraordinary life.
sentences.zh: 他有着极其不平凡的一生。

sentences.en: A lot of what we talked about last week, you know, was in that sort of fuzzy area between myth and history and fiction.
sentences.zh: 我们上周谈到的大部分内容，你知道的，都处于神话、历史和虚构之间的那种模糊地带。

sentences.en: But we know that, you know, he was exiled as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道，你知道的，他十几岁时就被流放了。

sentences.en: He went off to be a mercenary in Kievan Rus.
sentences.zh: 他去基辅罗斯当了雇佣兵。

sentences.en: He was a Varangian guard, messing around with the emperor and the empress, possible eye-gouging, comes back, snakes, snakes, great scenes, becomes king of Norway.
sentences.zh: 他曾是瓦兰吉卫队成员，跟皇帝和皇后瞎胡闹，可能还挖过别人的眼睛，后来回来，蛇，蛇，精彩的场面，最终成了挪威国王。

sentences.en: And we ended the Harold Hardrada series talking about how he earns the reputation, Hardrada.
sentences.zh: 我们在哈罗德·哈德拉达系列的结尾讨论了他如何赢得“哈德拉达”这个称号。

sentences.en: So, there's a kind of chilling ruthlessness to Harold Hardrada.
sentences.zh: 所以，哈罗德·哈德拉达身上有一种令人不寒而栗的冷酷无情。

sentences.en: Adam of Brayman, who we've mentioned before, called him the thunderbolt of the north.
sentences.zh: 我们之前提到过的不来梅的亚当称他为“北方霹雳”。

sentences.en: William of Poitiers, who we mentioned on Monday, said he was the strongest living man under the sun.
sentences.zh: 我们在周一提到过的普瓦捷的威廉说他是阳光下活着的最强壮的人。

sentences.en: So, even if you strip away the inventions of the sagas,
sentences.zh: 因此，即使你剥离掉那些萨迦传奇中的杜撰，

sentences.en: Harold Hardrada is a frighteningly ruthless, vengeful, effective, avaricious, impressive man.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·哈德拉达也是一个令人感到恐惧的冷酷、善于复仇、高效、贪婪且极具压迫感的人。

sentences.en: He is the distillation of the Viking ethos, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为，他就是维京人精神的精髓提炼。

sentences.en: And that's why his story makes such a wonderful conclusion to any history of the Vikings.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他的故事能成为任何维京人历史的绝佳结语。

sentences.en: And it's why he's such a perfect history for a saga of the kind that Snorri Sturluson and the other Icelandic writers have.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么他如此完美地契合了斯诺里·斯蒂德松和其他冰岛作家所钟爱的那种萨迦故事。

sentences.en: And one of the things that's fascinating about this particular episode is that we have a kind of first draft of history in the form of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.
sentences.zh: 这个特定故事令人着迷的一点在于，我们以《盎格鲁-萨克逊编年史》的形式拥有了一份历史的初稿。

sentences.en: Yes, we do.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: So, we talked about Tostick in the previous episode, and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle tells us that he has retreated from England in 1065,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在前一集里谈到了托斯蒂格，《盎格鲁-萨克逊编年史》告诉我们，他在1065年从英格兰撤退，

sentences.en: that he's gone to Flanders, that he then launches a raid on the Isle of Wight, that he then launches a raid on the Humber, and that he then goes to Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他去了佛兰德斯，接着对怀特岛发动了一场突袭，然后对亨伯河发动了一场突袭，之后去了苏格兰。

sentences.en: And that is all it tells us.
sentences.zh: 这就是它告诉我们的全部内容。

sentences.en: But the thing about Snorri's epic is that it fills in a lot of those details, whether accurately or not is up for debate, but certainly in a much more dramatic manner.
sentences.zh: 但斯诺里史诗的过人之处在于，它填补了许多细节，至于是否准确尚存争议，但它确实以一种极具戏剧性的方式呈现出来。

sentences.en: So, if we were doing this as an HBO series, we would start this episode with Harold in his hall in Vicken, which is near basically the Oslo region in Norway.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们要把它拍成一部HBO剧集，我们会以哈罗德在维肯的宫殿开场，那里基本上靠近挪威的奥斯陆地区。

sentences.en: And his days of war appear to be over.
sentences.zh: 而他的战争岁月似乎已经结束了。

sentences.en: He's fought this interminable war with the Danes that has basically ended in a stalemate.
sentences.zh: 他和丹麦人打了一场旷日持久的战争，基本上以僵局告终。

sentences.en: And you can sort of see how you would shoot the scene.
sentences.zh: 你大概能想象出这场戏会怎么拍。

sentences.en: He's sitting there at the end of his hall, grizzled.
sentences.zh: 他饱经风霜地坐在宫殿尽头。

sentences.en: The old wolf.
sentences.zh: 老狼。

sentences.en: The old wolf, exactly.
sentences.zh: 老狼，没错。

sentences.en: And one day in the summer of 1066, I mean, this must have been effectively what happened, a man walks into his hall, a man the sagas describe as, quote,
sentences.zh: 1066年夏天的某一天，我的意思是，这基本上就是当时发生的事情，一个人走进了他的宫殿，萨迦传奇将这个人描述为，引述如下，

sentences.en: a tall, strong man, a big talker and warlike with an enormous English moustache.
sentences.zh: “一个身材高大强壮、健谈好战、留着巨大英国式小胡子的人。”

sentences.en: I mean, the thing that's interesting about that description is that in the life of Edward the Confessor, which was commissioned by Tostig's sister, he's described as being short.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于这个描述有趣的一点是，在由托斯蒂格的姐姐委托撰写的《忏悔者爱德华生平》中，他被描述为个子矮小。

sentences.en: So, interesting contradiction there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里存在一个有趣的矛盾。

sentences.en: Maybe his sister didn't know what she was talking about.
sentences.zh: 也许他姐姐根本不知道自己在说什么。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: I'm going with the sagas, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我支持萨迦传奇的说法。

sentences.en: I'm always, by the way, in this episode, going to go with the sagas.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，在这集里我总是会支持萨迦传奇。

sentences.en: So, this is Tostig.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是托斯蒂格。

sentences.en: And as we described last time, Tostig is seething with resentment against his brother, Harold Godwinson,
sentences.zh: 正如我们上次所说，托斯蒂格对他的兄弟哈罗德·戈德温森充满了怨恨，

sentences.en: who he blames for his exile from England, the fact that Moorcar has become Earl of Northumbria, that everybody hates him, all of this.
sentences.zh: 他将自己被驱逐出英格兰、莫卡尔成为诺森布里亚伯爵以及所有人讨厌他等等一切，都归咎于这个兄弟。

sentences.en: Now, Tostig, in the last episode, had been raiding England.
sentences.zh: 现在，在上一集里，托斯蒂格一直在袭击英格兰。

sentences.en: He described him messing around in the Isle of Wight and the Humber and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 书中描述他在怀特岛和亨伯河一带瞎折腾之类的。

sentences.en: But I think it's pretty clear that after he's gone off to Scotland and he's been blown around, he's looking for something more than raiding.
sentences.zh: 但我认为很明显，在他去了苏格兰并在那里到处颠沛流离之后，他所谋求的已不仅仅是袭扰了。

sentences.en: I mean, by going to get help, he is signing up effectively to regime change in England.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，通过寻求援助，他实际上是在参与推翻英格兰政权的行动。

sentences.en: It's clear to him his brother's never going to take him back.
sentences.zh: 他很清楚，他的兄弟绝不会收留他。

sentences.en: There's no possibility of a rapprochement.
sentences.zh: 重修旧好已经毫无可能。

sentences.en: Now, if the sagas are to be believed, Harold Hardrada is not Tostig's first choice, because the sagas say, initially, he goes to see somebody you mentioned very briefly last time,
sentences.zh: 如果可以相信萨迦传奇的话，哈罗德·哈德拉达并不是托斯蒂格的首选，因为传奇记载，他最初去拜访了你上周极其简短提到过的一个人，

sentences.en: Svein of Denmark.
sentences.zh: 丹麦的斯韦恩。

sentences.en: And Tostig, in the sagas, says to him, why don't you come with me and win the country, win England, as Cnut, your mother's brother, did?
sentences.zh: 萨迦中的托斯蒂格对他说，你为什么不跟我一起来征服这个国家、征服英格兰，就像你母亲的兄弟克努特那样呢？

sentences.en: And I think this has the ring of absolute plausibility.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这绝对听起来合情合理。

sentences.en: Svein says, no, I'm not Cnut.
sentences.zh: 斯韦恩说，不，我不是克努特。

sentences.en: I don't have Cnut's capabilities.
sentences.zh: 我没有克努特的能力。

sentences.en: Only with difficulty can I defend my own Danish dominions against the Northmen, against the Norwegians, which is absolutely accurate.
sentences.zh: 我费了好大劲才能勉强保卫我自己的丹麦领地不被北方人、不被挪威人侵占，这绝对是实话。

sentences.en: Had Svein taken Tostig up on his offer and gone to England, there's no doubt in my mind that Harold Hardrada would have immediately invaded and conquered Denmark.
sentences.zh: 如果斯韦恩接受了托斯蒂格的提议并去了英格兰，我毫不怀疑哈罗德·哈德拉达会立刻入侵并征服丹麦。

sentences.en: So Svein would have been bonkers to take that up.
sentences.zh: 所以斯韦恩要是接受了才真是疯了。

sentences.en: Tostig, we're told, reacted contemptuously.
sentences.zh: 据说托斯蒂格对此反应轻蔑。

sentences.en: He says, I expected more of so gallant a man.
sentences.zh: 他说，我本对如此英勇之人抱有更高期望。

sentences.en: And I will look for help, he says, from a king who isn't frightened of a great enterprise as you are.
sentences.zh: 他说，我会去找一个不像你这样害怕宏图伟业的国王寻求帮助。

sentences.en: It has to be said that both the contemporanea sources and the sagas imply that Tostig does not have great interpersonal skills.
sentences.zh: 必须指出的是，无论是当代史料还是萨迦传奇都暗示托斯蒂格并不具备出色的社交能力。

sentences.en: He's not a charmer.
sentences.zh: 他不是个有魅力的人。

sentences.en: And to be fair, the record of history suggests that everybody despises Tostig.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，历史记载表明所有人都鄙视托斯蒂格。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But Tom?
sentences.zh: 但是汤姆？

sentences.en: Tostig will redeem himself at the end of this episode and behave, I think, in a very impressive and gallant way.
sentences.zh: 托斯蒂格将在本集结尾完成自我救赎，我认为他的表现将非常令人印象深刻且英勇无畏。

sentences.en: So now Tostig crosses the Skagorak to Vicken and he finds Harold Hardrada in his hall.
sentences.zh: 于是，托斯蒂格现在横渡斯卡格拉克海峡来到维肯，在宫殿里找到了哈罗德·哈德拉达。

sentences.en: Now, at first, Harold Hardrada, too, is dubious.
sentences.zh: 起初，哈罗德·哈德拉达也对此将信将疑。

sentences.en: You talked last time about how some of William of Normandy's advisors said,
sentences.zh: 你上次谈到诺曼底公爵威廉的一些顾问曾说，

sentences.en: England, really?
sentences.zh: 英格兰？真的吗？

sentences.en: That is a tough nut to crack.
sentences.zh: 那可是一块难啃的骨头。

sentences.en: That is a hell of a gamble.
sentences.zh: 那可是一场天大的赌博。

sentences.en: And Hardrada hesitates.
sentences.zh: 于是哈德拉达犹豫了。

sentences.en: We're told, the king replied that the Northmen had no great desire for a campaign in England.
sentences.zh: 据说国王回答说，北方人对去英格兰打仗并没有多大兴趣。

sentences.en: People say that the English are not to be trusted.
sentences.zh: 人们说英国人是信不过的。

sentences.en: Who says that?
sentences.zh: 谁说的这番话？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, this is outrageous.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这太离谱了。

sentences.en: Everyone knows that an Englishman's word is his boss.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，英国人一言既出，驷马难追。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: This is fools in Norway, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以说这是挪威人的愚蠢表现。

sentences.en: Idiots.
sentences.zh: 一群白痴。

sentences.en: Remember, Harold Hardrada has never been to England, so he knows not whereof he speaks.
sentences.zh: 记住，哈罗德·哈德拉达从未去过英格兰，所以他这是在信口雌黄。

sentences.en: Yeah, true.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And Tostig says, hold on.
sentences.zh: 然后托斯蒂格说，等等。

sentences.en: Remember, you have a claim to the English throne.
sentences.zh: 记住，你对英格兰王位拥有继承权。

sentences.en: He reminds Hardrada that a quarter of a century earlier, during the succession crisis after the death of Canute,
sentences.zh: 他提醒哈德拉达，就在四分之一世纪前，在克努特死后的继承危机期间，

sentences.en: there was this story that Hartha Canute and Hardrada's brother Magnus had done a deal that whichever of them died without an heir would inherit the other's kingdom,
sentences.zh: 曾有这样一桩传闻：哈达·克努特和哈德拉达的兄弟马格努斯曾达成一项协议，他们两人中无论谁死后没有子嗣，都将继承对方的王国，

sentences.en: all of his kingdoMs.
sentences.zh: 继承他所有的王国。

sentences.en: And Tostig says to Hardrada, Magnus was your brother, and you've inherited that claim.
sentences.zh: 托斯蒂格对哈德拉达说，马格努斯是你的兄弟，你已经继承了那一权利。

sentences.en: Edward the confessor has died without an heir, and under the terms of that deal, England is yours.
sentences.zh: 忏悔者爱德华死后无嗣，根据那项协议的条款，英格兰就是你的了。

sentences.en: Now, whether they'd really made that deal, it's not written down anywhere, so who knows?
sentences.zh: 至于他们是否真的达成过那项协议，任何地方都没有文字记录，所以谁知道呢？

sentences.en: But it's convenient for Hardrada.
sentences.zh: 但这很符合哈德拉达的心意。

sentences.en: And Tostig goes on, according to the sagas, if you want it, England is yours.
sentences.zh: 而根据萨迦传奇的记载，托斯蒂格接着说道，如果你想要，英格兰就是你的。

sentences.en: I can talk most of the lords there into supporting you.
sentences.zh: 我能说服那里的大多数领主支持你。

sentences.en: That, as we know of Tostig, is a dubious claim, to say the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 正如我们对托斯蒂格的了解，保守地说，这是一个极其靠不住的承诺。

sentences.en: Tostig goes on, and he appeals to Hardrada's vanity.
sentences.zh: 托斯蒂格继续说着，他开始迎合哈德拉达的虚荣心。

sentences.en: Everybody says that never in all the Northlands has there been a warrior king to compare with you.
sentences.zh: 所有人都说，整个北方从未有过能与你相比的英雄国王。

sentences.en: So it seems odd to me that you spent 15 years trying to conquer Denmark, and yet you shrink from the chance of ruling England when it is yours for the taking.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，你花了15年时间试图征服丹麦，却在统治英格兰的机会唾手可得时退缩了，这实在有些奇怪。

sentences.en: Oh, he's subtle there, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 哦，他在这里处理得真巧妙，不是吗？

sentences.en: Now, the sagas then say that Harold and Tostig talked long and frequently together, which undoubtedly they must have done.
sentences.zh: 根据传奇记载，哈拉尔和托斯蒂格曾长时间且频繁地交谈，他们确实毫无疑问地这样做了。

sentences.en: And Harold has to weigh this up, right?
sentences.zh: 哈拉尔必须权衡这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: Because this is a gamble.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一场赌博。

sentences.en: Now, until this moment, he has never shown the slightest interest in England.
sentences.zh: 然而在此之前，他对英格兰从未表现出哪怕一丝兴趣。

sentences.en: And people who listen to our Harold Hardrada two-parter will know that basically all his career was spent in the East, not the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 听过我们关于哈拉尔·哈德拉达两集节目的人就会知道，他基本上整个职业生涯都在东方度过，而不是西方。

sentences.en: He's always looked EaSt.
sentences.zh: 他的目光一直投向东方。

sentences.en: Because there are two paths to wealth in the Viking world, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 因为在维京人的世界里，通往财富的途径有两条，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: England or continental neighbourhood, basically, by this point.
sentences.zh: 基本上到了这个时候，就是英格兰或欧洲大陆周边。

sentences.en: So this is a novelty for him.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他是件新鲜事。

sentences.en: He's never really thought about England before.
sentences.zh: 他以前从未真正考虑过英格兰。

sentences.en: Some of his chief advisors, we're told, said, look, you can do anything.
sentences.zh: 据说他的一些首席谋士曾说，看吧，你什么都能做到。

sentences.en: You're the thunderbolt of the North.
sentences.zh: 你是北方的霹雳。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Let's go for it.
sentences.zh: 我们大干一场吧。

sentences.en: Others, and this echoes again what the Normans said to William, others again said that England was difficult to attack, that it was very full of people,
sentences.zh: 另一些人则说，英格兰很难进攻，那里人口众多——这与诺曼人对威廉说的话如出一辙——

sentences.en: and that the men-at-arms were so brave that one of them was better than two of Harold's best men,
sentences.zh: 而且他们的精兵强将如此勇敢，其中一人抵得上哈拉尔麾下最好的两个人，

sentences.en: which actually, again, bears out what you were saying last time, that the English are generally underrated.
sentences.zh: 这其实再次印证了你上次所说的话，即英格兰人普遍被低估了。

sentences.en: We tend to think, oh, the English were rubbish because they were very peaceable.
sentences.zh: 我们往往会想，哦，英格兰人很逊，因为他们爱好和平。

sentences.en: But actually, they're more formidable than you think.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们比你想象的要可怕得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, and to look at it from the Viking point of view, Viking armies keep going over to England.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果从维京人的角度来看，维京军队一直在不断前往英格兰。

sentences.en: They keep battering it, conquering it, draining it if it's silver, and still it endures and comes back kind of stronger than ever.
sentences.zh: 他们不断攻击、征服、榨取银子，而英格兰依然挺了过来，甚至变得比以往更加强大。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: So Harold sits and thinks about it, and eventually he decides he'll do it.
sentences.zh: 因此，哈拉尔坐下来思考了一番，最终他决定干了。

sentences.en: And I think there are three reasons why.
sentences.zh: 我认为原因有三个。

sentences.en: Number one is the great traditional Viking reason, which I think does then sort of cement his last Viking reputation, and that is basically money.
sentences.zh: 第一点是维京人传统的宏大理由，我认为这确实巩固了他最后的维京声誉，那就是金钱。

sentences.en: He has had terrible trouble in Norway raising taxes to pay for his wars, hence the name Hardrada, because he's basically been harrying people who won't pay their taxes.
sentences.zh: 他在挪威筹集税款来支付战争费用时遇到了极大的麻烦，这也是他被称为“严酷者（Hardrada）”的原因，因为他基本上一直在对那些拒绝交税的人大加搜刮。

sentences.en: But England, as we've established, is very, very rich.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们已经确定的那样，英格兰非常非常富有。

sentences.en: And even if he didn't get the crown, imagine that he lands, there's a lot of battles, there's a kind of stalemate, a little bit like it was with, you know,
sentences.zh: 即使他没有夺得王位，想象一下他登陆了，经历了无数场战斗，陷入某种僵局，有点像是，你知道的，

sentences.en: Svein Fortbeard and Cnut in the early days.
sentences.zh: 早期时期的斯韦恩·福克伯德和克努特那样。

sentences.en: He might just go home with loads of Dane geld.
sentences.zh: 他可能带着大量的丹麦金（Dane geld）就回国了。

sentences.en: The English would buy him off.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人会用钱把他打发走。

sentences.en: The English would buy him off.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人会花钱消灾。

sentences.en: So that's the, you know, that could be a worst case scenario.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这可能会是最坏的情况。

sentences.en: He doesn't think he's going to die.
sentences.zh: 他不认为自己会死。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not the worst case scenario, actually, as it will turn out, is it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际结果证明，这其实并不是最坏的情况，对吧？

sentences.en: But yes, I mean, that's what he could get.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，我是说，这就是他可能得到的。

sentences.en: Then I think there's a geopolitical reason.
sentences.zh: 其次，我认为还有一个地缘政治原因。

sentences.en: It's very clear that Harald has always wanted to, you know, Norway's not enough for him.
sentences.zh: 很明显，哈拉尔一直想要，你知道的，挪威对他来说已经不够了。

sentences.en: Basically, if you're a Norwegian or Danish king, your ambition is obviously to try to be the next
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你是一个挪威或丹麦国王，你的雄心壮志显然是努力成为下一个

sentences.en: Cnut, to build a kind of North Sea empire.
sentences.zh: 克努特，建立某种北海帝国。

sentences.en: It would make complete sense that you might want to try to do that.
sentences.zh: 你想要尝试这样做完全合情合理。

sentences.en: And I guess Harald Hardrada has seen Yaroslav the Wise, the great king of Kiev, and he's seen the emperor in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 我想哈拉尔·哈德拉达见识过基辅伟大的国王智者雅罗斯拉夫，也见过君士坦丁堡的皇帝。

sentences.en: So he has a sense, perhaps, that Norway is a slightly shrunken and impoverished stage compared to those.
sentences.zh: 所以与那些地方相比，他或许会觉得挪威是一个有些萎缩且贫瘠的舞台。

sentences.en: He's been playing for Real Madrid, and now he's managing Burnley.
sentences.zh: 他以前是在为皇家马德里效力，现在却在执教伯恩利。

sentences.en: And he probably thinks to himself, you know, ideally, I'd be managing a bigger club.
sentences.zh: 他心里大概会想，理想情况下，我应该去执教一家更大的俱乐部。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the third thing, I think, is psychological.
sentences.zh: 第三点，我认为是心理层面的。

sentences.en: And there's no reason to doubt the evidence of the sagas that Harald Hardrada is a very restless,
sentences.zh: 没有任何理由怀疑萨迦（sagas）中的记录，即哈拉尔·哈德拉达是一个极度焦躁、

sentences.en: warlike man who basically, he's a bit like Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 好战的人，他基本上有点像亚历山大大帝。

sentences.en: He doesn't like building bridges and discussing tax returns.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢修建桥梁和讨论税单。

sentences.en: What he really likes doing is fighting people.
sentences.zh: 他真正喜欢做的是跟人打仗。

sentences.en: But also, unlike Alexander the Great, he's now 50.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，与亚历山大大帝不同的是，他现在已经五十岁了。

sentences.en: And so he's prone to a massive midlife crisis, I guess.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，他很容易陷入严重的中年危机。

sentences.en: Massive midlife crisis.
sentences.zh: 严重的中年危机。

sentences.en: Snorri says, he yearned to conquer new realMs.
sentences.zh: 斯诺里（Snorri）说，他渴望征服新的国度。

sentences.en: And again, if you're doing this as your TV series, he's sitting there on his throne, grizzled one last time.
sentences.zh: 同样，如果你把这拍成电视剧，他就会最后一次饱经风霜地坐在王座上。

sentences.en: Will you join me?
sentences.zh: 你愿意加入我吗？

sentences.en: You know, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，诸如此类的情节。

sentences.en: So the orders go out.
sentences.zh: 于是，命令下达了。

sentences.en: They assemble a fleet in the western fjords.
sentences.zh: 他们在西部峡湾集结了一支舰队。

sentences.en: We're told 200 longships and 100 transports.
sentences.zh: 据说有两百艘长船和一百艘运输船。

sentences.en: So if you assume about 50 to 60 men per longship, that would be about 10,000 men.
sentences.zh: 如果你按每艘长船大约五十到六十人来算，那大约是一万人。

sentences.en: That's plausible because that's similar to the force that he threw against Denmark.
sentences.zh: 这很合情合理，因为这与他派去攻打丹麦的兵力规模相似。

sentences.en: It's actually bigger than the fleet that Canute used to conquer England in 1016.
sentences.zh: 它实际上比克努特在1016年征服英格兰时使用的舰队还要大。

sentences.en: And I guess that like William's invasion force, which is massing at this very moment on the north coast of France,
sentences.zh: 我想，就像威廉的入侵部队此时此刻正在法国北部海岸集结一样，

sentences.en: Harald's name and reputation is a huge draw.
sentences.zh: 哈拉尔的名字和声誉有着巨大的号召力。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: If you're a young man from Norway, Sweden, Denmark, or indeed New East or from Flanders or wherever it might be, and the word has gone out,
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个来自挪威、瑞典、丹麦，或是新东方（New East）、法兰德斯或其他什么地方的年轻男子，当消息传开：

sentences.en: Harald's sails again.
sentences.zh: 哈拉尔再次扬帆起航了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's like something from a western, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就像是西部片里的情节，对吧？

sentences.en: The dragon boats shall roar at last time as the sun sets in the weSt.
sentences.zh: 当太阳在西方落下时，龙船终于要发出怒吼。

sentences.en: It's Theoden in the Lord of the Rings, right?
sentences.zh: 就像《指环王》里的希奥顿（Theoden），对吧？

sentences.en: One last time.
sentences.zh: 最后一次。

sentences.en: You know, with all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: So, the fleet is assembled.
sentences.zh: 于是，舰队集结完毕。

sentences.en: Before leaving, he goes to visit the shrine of his late brothers, St. Olaf, in a place called Nidaros, which is today Trondheim.
sentences.zh: 在出发之前，他去参观了他已故的兄弟圣奥拉夫的圣陵，地点在一个叫尼达罗斯（Nidaros）的地方，也就是今天的特隆赫姆。

sentences.en: And St. Olaf has already been turned into a slightly implausible patron saint of Norway as a way of buttressing the Hadrada dynasty regime.
sentences.zh: 圣奥拉夫已经被塑造成一个略显勉强的挪威主保圣人，以此来巩固哈德拉达王朝的统治。

sentences.en: And he supposedly, I mean, why you would do this,
sentences.zh: 据说他——我是说，你为什么会这么做，

sentences.en: God knows you'll know more about this than me, Tom.
sentences.zh: 天知道，汤姆，你肯定比我更清楚。

sentences.en: He trims the hair and nails of the body of his brother, and then bizarrely throws the key of the tomb into the river.
sentences.zh: 他修剪了他兄弟遗体的头发和指甲，然后匪夷所思地把墓穴的钥匙扔进了河里。

sentences.en: Well, Otto III, in the millennial year, the year 1000, had done the same for Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在千禧年，即公元1000年，奥托三世也曾为查理曼大帝做过同样的事。

sentences.en: He'd gone down into Charlemagne's tomb and trimmed his nails.
sentences.zh: 他曾进入查理曼大帝的陵墓并修剪了他的指甲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, it's obviously a thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，这显然是一种仪式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, a very bad blow for Hadrada is that just as they're preparing to sail, his men are afflicted by a series of terrible dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 现在，对哈德拉达来说一个沉重的打击是，就在他们准备起航时，他的手下们遭遇了一连串可怕的噩梦。

sentences.en: And, Tom, you may scoff at this, but I have no reason to doubt that this happened.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你可能会对此嗤之以鼻，但我没有理由怀疑这件事没有发生过。

sentences.en: So, first of all, there's a man called Geard, and he dreamed of seeing ravens perched on the prows of all their longships,
sentences.zh: 首先，有一个叫盖尔德（Geard）的人，他梦见乌鸦栖息在他们所有长船的船头上，

sentences.en: and a sinister witch wife singing that all the men would soon be a feast for crows.
sentences.zh: 还有一个阴险的巫婆唱着歌，说所有人很快都会成为乌鸦的盘中餐。

sentences.en: That's not good, is it?
sentences.zh: 这可不是什么好兆头，对吧？

sentences.en: Unfortunately, there's another bloke called Thord, and he says, well, he's also had a dream.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，还有另一个叫托德（Thord）的家伙说，他同样也做了个梦。

sentences.en: He saw two armies lined up for battle in the fields of England, another of these witch wives riding between them on a wolf, and I quote,
sentences.zh: 他看见两支军队在英格兰的田野上列阵准备战斗，另一个巫婆骑着一匹狼在两军之间穿梭，我引用原话：

sentences.en: The wolf had a man's carcass in his mouth, and the blood was dripping from his jaws, and when he'd eaten one body, she, the witch wife,
sentences.zh: “那头狼嘴里叼着一具男人的尸体，鲜血从它的颌下滴落，当它吃完一具尸体后，她——那个巫婆——

sentences.en: threw another corpse into his mouth until he swallowed them all.
sentences.zh: 便把另一具尸体扔进它嘴里，直到它把它们全吞下去。”

sentences.en: Again, I mean, it's, you know, it could be the English.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，这，你知道的，可能暗示着英格兰人。

sentences.en: But then, unfortunately, the crowning dream,
sentences.zh: 但随后，不幸的是，最高潮的噩梦来了，

sentences.en: Harold himself has a dream that his brother Olaf, with his nails nicely trimmed, turns up during the night wearing the same armour that he had worn
sentences.zh: 哈拉尔本人做了一个梦，他的兄弟奥拉夫指甲修剪得整整齐齐，在夜里现身了，身上穿着他在

sentences.en: at the fatal battle of Sticklastad, which we did in our Harold Hardrada series.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂克拉斯塔德（Sticklastad）那场致命战役中穿过的同一套盔甲——我们在哈拉尔·哈德拉达系列节目中讲过那场战役。

sentences.en: Well, he's chopped to pieces, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 好吧，他被砍成碎块了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Olaf, bleeding, turns up in this armour and sings to him,
sentences.zh: 所以浑身是血的奥拉夫穿着这套盔甲出现，并向他唱道：

sentences.en: Thy death is near, thy corpse I fear, the crow will feed the witch wife's steed.
sentences.zh: “你的死期将近，我担心你的尸体，乌鸦将喂养巫婆的坐骑。”

sentences.en: So this is a bad, bad development for Harold Hardrada.
sentences.zh: 所以这对哈拉尔·哈德拉达来说是一个极其糟糕的发展。

sentences.en: You can imagine him shivering as he stands at the prow of his ship.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象他站在船头时瑟瑟发抖的样子。

sentences.en: You think he would shiver?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他会发抖吗？

sentences.en: He would shiver.
sentences.zh: 他会发抖的。

sentences.en: He'd give a little imperceptible shiver, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他会微微地、不易察觉地颤抖一下。

sentences.en: An internal shiver.
sentences.zh: 一种内心的颤抖。

sentences.en: He'd draw his bear skin, you know, his wolf skin cloak tighter around him.
sentences.zh: 他会把熊皮，你知道的，把狼皮斗篷裹得更紧一些。

sentences.en: He would gaze back at the dark forest of Norway and then his face would set and he would gaze at the grey, steely waters of the North Sea and set sail for England.
sentences.zh: 他会凝视着挪威幽暗的森林，然后面色紧绷，凝视着北海那钢灰色、冰冷的水面，起航前往英格兰。

sentences.en: This is literally what happened.
sentences.zh: 这真的就是发生的事情。

sentences.en: So August 1066, it's now or never they set sail.
sentences.zh: 所以那是1066年8月，时不我待，他们扬帆起航了。

sentences.en: Now, at first, they seem to have headed northwest towards Orkney.
sentences.zh: 起初，他们似乎朝着西北方向的奥克尼群岛驶去。

sentences.en: And Orkney is part of Harold's empire.
sentences.zh: 奥克尼群岛是哈拉尔帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: And we are told by Heims Kringler, the King Harold saga, that there he collected more men and he left.
sentences.zh: 根据《海姆斯克林格拉》（Heims Kringla，即《国王哈拉尔萨迦》）的记载，他在那里招募了更多人，然后离开了。

sentences.en: The saga says he left Queen Elisif.
sentences.zh: 萨迦记载说他留下了伊丽丝芙（Elisif）王后。

sentences.en: So she's the one from Yaroslav's daughter.
sentences.zh: 也就是雅罗斯拉夫的女儿。

sentences.en: And her daughters, Maria and Ingergerd, in Orkney.
sentences.zh: 还有她的女儿们玛丽亚和英格盖德，留在了奥克尼。

sentences.en: But historians now think that's unlikely, that she might have been dead by this point anyway.
sentences.zh: 但历史学家现在认为这种说法不太可能，她当时可能已经去世了。

sentences.en: And that actually he had a second wife called Tora and that maybe it was her who he left in Orkney.
sentences.zh: 实际上他还有第二个妻子叫托拉（Tora），留在奥克尼的可能反而是她。

sentences.en: Anyway, we don't need to worry about them.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我们不需要过多担心她们。

sentences.en: And it's interesting because there's a 12th century English chronicler, so that's well before Snorri, who says that Tostig, who has spent the whole summer, you know, presumably
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，有一位12世纪的英格兰编年史家——这远在斯诺里之前——说托斯蒂格度过了整个夏天，你知道的，大概是

sentences.en: having come back from seeing Harold Hardrada hanging out with Malcolm of Scotland, that he has already been joined by ships from Orkney, presumably sent by Hardrada.
sentences.zh: 在拜访了和苏格兰国王马尔科姆厮混的哈拉尔·哈德拉达并返回之后，奥克尼群岛的船只——很可能是哈德拉达派去的——已经与他汇合了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's slightly confusing where Tostig is at this point because the sagas give different explanations.
sentences.zh: 是的，托斯蒂格此时身在何处有点让人困惑，因为萨迦给出了不同的解释。

sentences.en: But Tostig is definitely doing something up in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 但托斯蒂格肯定在苏格兰那边进行着某些活动。

sentences.en: He's with Malcolm.
sentences.zh: 他和马尔科姆在一起。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle says.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史就是这么说的。

sentences.en: So Harold now turns south.
sentences.zh: 于是哈拉尔转而向南。

sentences.en: He sails down the east coast of Scotland towards the ancient kingdom of Northumbria.
sentences.zh: 他沿着苏格兰东海岸南下，驶向古代诺森布里亚王国。

sentences.en: Of course, the part of England with very, very strong Scandinavian roots and the Scandinavian traditions.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是英格兰与斯堪的纳维亚有着极其深厚根基和传统的地区。

sentences.en: And in the middle of September, Hardrada makes landfall on the coast at a place called, then called Cliffland, Cliffland, what we would now call Cleveland, North Yorkshire.
sentences.zh: 在九月中旬，哈德拉达在当时被称为克利夫兰（Cliffland）、也就是我们现在所称的北约克郡克利夫兰（Cleveland）的海岸登陆。

sentences.en: And this is very Danish territory.
sentences.zh: 这完全是丹麦人的领地。

sentences.en: So the first villages that he comes to, which are now suburbs of Middlesbrough, today they are Ormsby, Stainsby, Tollsby.
sentences.zh: 所以他到达的第一个村庄——如今已是米德尔斯堡的郊区——分别是今天的奥姆斯比（Ormsby）、斯坦斯比（Stainsby）、托尔斯比（Tollsby）。

sentences.en: They are Danish names.
sentences.zh: 这些都是丹麦语地名。

sentences.en: They are named after Vikings called Orm, Stain, Toll.
sentences.zh: 它们是以名叫奥姆（Orm）、斯坦（Stain）、托尔（Toll）的维京人名字命名的。

sentences.en: And the people there were told offered Hardrada no resistance.
sentences.zh: 据说那里的居民对哈德拉达没有进行任何抵抗。

sentences.en: Now that may be...
sentences.zh: 这或许……

sentences.en: I mean, you wouldn't, would you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，换作你也不会抵抗，对吧？

sentences.en: You wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 你不会的。

sentences.en: But also, these are places where they probably have trade with Scandinavia, where the arrival
sentences.zh: 而且，这些地方可能与斯堪的纳维亚有着贸易往来，在那里，斯堪的纳维亚人的到来

sentences.en: of Scandinavians is not maybe as terrifying and outlandish as it would be had they landed in Devon, let us say.
sentences.zh: 或许并不像他们如果在德文郡登陆那样令人感到恐怖和陌生。

sentences.en: So they do a bit of messing around there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在那里稍微逗留了一阵。

sentences.en: Then they sail 40 miles south to a place called Skardie's Fort, Skardaborg, which is named after a brilliant man called Thorgil Skardie, Thorgil's the hair-lipped.
sentences.zh: 然后他们向南航行了40英里，来到一个叫做斯卡迪堡（Skardie's Fort / Skardaborg）的地方，这个名字是以一个杰出的人——缺唇的索吉尔（Thorgil Skardie）命名的。

sentences.en: And Skardie's Fort, Skardaborg, we now call Scarborough.
sentences.zh: 而斯卡迪堡（Skardaborg），我们现在称之为斯卡伯勒（Scarborough）。

sentences.en: So they land at Scarborough.
sentences.zh: 于是他们在斯卡伯勒登陆。

sentences.en: Now, Scarborough is a larger town.
sentences.zh: 现在，斯卡伯勒是一个更大的城镇。

sentences.en: It's fortified.
sentences.zh: 这里有防御工事。

sentences.en: And the people here clearly seem to have felt more English because they actually do try to resist Hardrada.
sentences.zh: 这里的居民显然觉得自己更有英国人的认同感，因为他们实实在在地试图抵抗哈拉德拉。

sentences.en: Hardrada takes the town anyway, and we're told by the saga, the Northmen killed many people there and took all the booty they could lay hold of.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，哈拉德拉还是攻占了这座城镇。据萨迦记载，诺斯人杀害了那里的许多人，并抢走了他们所能拿走的所有战利品。

sentences.en: There was nothing left for the Englishmen now if they would preserve their lives but to submit to King Harald, and thus he subdued the country wherever he came.
sentences.zh: 对于英国人来说，如果他们想保全性命，除了向哈拉 Harald 国王投降外，别无选择，因此他无论走到哪里都征服了这片土地。

sentences.en: So in other words, he's made an example of Scarborough.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他拿斯卡伯勒杀鸡儆猴了。

sentences.en: He has looted it, sacked it, and this sends a message to all the towns of eastern, northeastern
sentences.zh: 他洗劫了这里，劫掠了这里，这向东方、东北方的所有城镇发出了一条信息

sentences.en: England.
sentences.zh: 英格兰。

sentences.en: You stand in my way, and I will hammer you.
sentences.zh: 你挡我的路，我就会狠狠地收拾你。

sentences.en: But you do right by me, and I'll do right by you.
sentences.zh: 但你对我好，我也会对你好。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So now he turns into the mouth of the Humber, and by this point, we can be pretty sure he has joined forces with Tostig.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他驶入了亨伯河口，到这个时候，我们可以相当确定他已经与托斯蒂格会合了。

sentences.en: And Tostig has some Flemish mercenaries, probably, and he definitely has men from Scotland, from
sentences.zh: 托斯蒂格可能有一些弗兰德斯雇佣兵，而且他绝对拥有来自苏格兰的人，来自

sentences.en: King Malcolm.
sentences.zh: 马尔科姆国王。

sentences.en: Tostig has already sailed up the Humber once already this year, 1066, and it's a reminder of the way that for, if you have any kind of Scandinavian inheritance of invasion, the
sentences.zh: 今年（1066年）托斯蒂格已经顺着亨伯河向上航行过一次了，这提醒人们，如果你有任何斯堪的纳维亚式的入侵传统，

sentences.en: Humber is where you go.
sentences.zh: 亨伯河就是你的必经之路。

sentences.en: It's like a great dagger pointed into the vitals of Middle England.
sentences.zh: 它就像一把直刺英格兰中部心脏的巨型匕首。

sentences.en: And this is a standard thing, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一贯的做法，对吧？

sentences.en: This is not unusual.
sentences.zh: 这并不罕见。

sentences.en: So far, Hardrada is following the playbook that so many Vikings have done so often.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，哈拉德拉遵循的正是无数维京人屡试不爽的剧本。

sentences.en: He probably has about 12,000 men at this point.
sentences.zh: 此时他手下大约有 12,000 人。

sentences.en: This includes his own son, Olaf, and Tostig's son, who's called Schooley.
sentences.zh: 其中包括他的亲生儿子奥拉夫，以及托斯蒂格名叫舒利的儿子。

sentences.en: They go up the Humber, and then they turn into the River Ouse.
sentences.zh: 他们沿亨伯河而上，然后拐入了乌斯河。

sentences.en: People remember how they'd use the networks of rivers in what are now Russia and Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 人们还记得他们当年如何在如今的俄罗斯和乌克兰境内利用河流网。

sentences.en: Now they're using the network of rivers in northern England.
sentences.zh: 现在他们正在利用英格兰北部的河流网。

sentences.en: And they row up the Ouse northwards until they reach the village of Rickle, which is 10 miles from York.
sentences.zh: 他们向北划着船沿乌斯河而上，直到抵达距离约克 10 英里的里克尔村。

sentences.en: Now, so far, everything Harold has done has made complete sense, has been very well planned.
sentences.zh: 现在，到目前为止，哈罗德所做的一切都完全合乎情理，而且计划得非常周密。

sentences.en: He has gone for the area of England that has the longest and deepest Scandinavian connections.
sentences.zh: 他直奔英格兰斯堪的纳维亚联系最久、最深的地区。

sentences.en: He doesn't seem to be just interested in raiding.
sentences.zh: 他似乎不仅仅对掠夺感兴趣。

sentences.en: I think he's probably serious about conquest, which is why he's going for York, because York is one of the two biggest urban prizes, really.
sentences.zh: 我认为他可能是在认真考虑征服，这就是他进攻约克的原因，因为约克确实是两个最大的城市战利品之一。

sentences.en: London is the only one that compares.
sentences.zh: 只有伦敦能与之相比。

sentences.en: There's this formerly Jorvik, massive Scandinavian heritage.
sentences.zh: 这里曾经是约尔维克，拥有庞大的斯堪的纳维亚传统。

sentences.en: It would have been the capital of Eric Bloodaxe.
sentences.zh: 它曾是血斧埃里克的首都。

sentences.en: There are a lot of people there who would have Scandinavian family connections, roots, and so on, trading connections.
sentences.zh: 那里有很多人拥有斯堪的纳维亚的家庭联系、根基等等，还有贸易联系。

sentences.en: There's also an archbishop, so quite convenient.
sentences.zh: 这里还有一位大主教，所以相当方便。

sentences.en: And of course, they crack out enormous turds, mighty Viking turds.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们拉出了巨大的粪便，强悍的维京粪便。

sentences.en: I think the largest turd, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想这是最大的粪便吧？

sentences.en: The largest fossil turd ever found, something like that.
sentences.zh: 有史以来发现的最大的化石粪便，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So a terrifying place.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个可怕的地方。

sentences.en: Slightly more excitingly, it also has a mint.
sentences.zh: 稍微令人兴奋一点的是，它还有一个造币厂。

sentences.en: So it's one of the only places, it's the only mint in northern England.
sentences.zh: 所以它是少数几个地方之一，是英格兰北部唯一的造币厂。

sentences.en: So if you take York, you're taking a proper seat of kind of royal authority.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你占领了约克，你就占据了真正的王权宝座。

sentences.en: Anyway, York is guarded by the two northernmost earls, and we've talked about them a lot.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，约克由最北部的两位伯爵把守，我们经常谈到他们。

sentences.en: They are Morkar, the Earl of Northumbria, and Edwin, Earl of Mercia.
sentences.zh: 他们是诺森比亚伯爵莫卡尔，以及麦西亚伯爵埃德温。

sentences.en: They are the grandsons of Leofric.
sentences.zh: 他们是莱夫里克的孙子。

sentences.en: They are the dynasty that have been the great counterweight to the Godwinsons.
sentences.zh: 他们是与戈德温森家族分庭抗礼的伟大王朝。

sentences.en: And they're now the brothers-in-law of Harold Godwinson.
sentences.zh: 而他们现在是哈罗德·戈德温森的小舅子。

sentences.en: So they are now loyal to Harold as king.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在效忠于国王哈罗德。

sentences.en: Now, they are both much younger than Hardrada and much less battle-hardened.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们两人的年纪都比哈拉德拉小得多，而且远没有那么饱经战阵。

sentences.en: They're both in their 20s.
sentences.zh: 他们都二十出头。

sentences.en: And it may be that Hardrada thought they would come to a deal, that they would panic and run away, that they would surrender.
sentences.zh: 哈拉德拉可能认为他们会妥协，他们会惊慌失措并逃跑，他们会投降。

sentences.en: But they don't.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有。

sentences.en: Now, an interesting thing here is, why don't they stay in York?
sentences.zh: 这里有一个有趣的问题：他们为什么不留在约克？

sentences.en: Because York has stone walls that are built on kind of Roman foundations.
sentences.zh: 因为约克的石墙是建立在某种罗马地基上的。

sentences.en: Everybody knows the one thing the Vikings don't like doing is besieging towns.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，维京人最不喜欢做的事就是围攻城镇。

sentences.en: They're not terribly good at it.
sentences.zh: 他们在这方面并不太擅长。

sentences.en: They don't enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢这样做。

sentences.en: Why don't Edwin and Morkar just stay in York and wait for Harold Godwinson to come with his army and relieve them?
sentences.zh: 埃德温和莫卡尔为什么不直接留在约克，等待哈罗德·戈德温森带着他的军队来支援他们呢？

sentences.en: The obvious answer is that, as you described last time, Harold Godwinson has been waiting on the south coast for ages for the Normans.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的答案是，正如你上次所描述的那样，哈罗德·戈德温森已经在南部海岸等待诺曼人很久了。

sentences.en: And his men have become restless, and he has released them to go off and bring in the harveSt.
sentences.zh: 他的手下已经开始焦躁不安，他已经准许他们离开去收割庄稼了。

sentences.en: So Edwin and Morkar probably think, first of all, that his men are all gone, so maybe he's not going to come and relieve us anyway.
sentences.zh: 因此埃德温和莫卡尔可能首先认为，他的人都走了，所以也许他无论如何都不会来支援我们了。

sentences.en: But crucially, our own men have not brought in our harvest, so we don't have a lot of food in York.
sentences.zh: 但至关重要的是，我们自己的人也没有收割庄稼，所以在约克我们没有大量的食物。

sentences.en: The city is reliant on what small stocks of food we have.
sentences.zh: 这座城市依靠我们仅有的一点点食物存货维系。

sentences.en: And if we stay cooped up in York, Hardrada's men, they'll ravage the fields or they'll eat all of the harvest themselves, and we will starve.
sentences.zh: 如果我们一直蜷缩在约克，哈拉德拉的手下就会蹂躏田野，或者他们会把所有的庄稼吃光，而我们就会挨饿。

sentences.en: So we basically have no choice but to force the issue.
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上别无选择，只能背水一战。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They are bold, these pups.
sentences.zh: 这些小伙子胆子不小。

sentences.en: Is that how would Hardrada join us?
sentences.zh: 哈拉德拉是怎么加入我们的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So now we come to Wednesday, the 20th of September.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来到 9 月 20 日星期三。

sentences.en: So that morning, Harold and Tostig are marching north along the River Ouse towards the hamlet of Fulford, which is now a suburb of York, southern suburb of York.
sentences.zh: 那天早上，哈罗德和托斯蒂格沿乌斯河向北行军，朝着富尔福德小村庄前进，该村现在是约克的郊区，约克的南部郊区。

sentences.en: And at Fulford, they find, according to the sagas, they find their road blocked by a shield wall of about 4,000 men.
sentences.zh: 根据萨迦的记载，在富尔福德，他们发现道路被一堵约有 4,000 人组成的盾墙挡住了。

sentences.en: And these are Edwin and Morkar's house gulls, so in other words, they're trained professional soldiers, and they're sort of levies.
sentences.zh: 这些是埃德温和莫卡尔的近卫军，换句话说，他们是训练有素的职业士兵，还有一些征召兵。

sentences.en: And a real ragtag, you know, farm, people with pitchforks.

sentences.zh: 还有他承诺的女婿爱因斯坦。

sentences.en: And then the other 8,000, he and Tosti will take them to go and get the hostages and the supplies and things.
sentences.zh: 然后剩下的8000人，他和托斯蒂将带着他们去获取人质、补给以及其他东西。

sentences.en: And we know that it's unseasonably warm.
sentences.zh: 我们知道天气异常温暖。

sentences.en: So the Heimskringler, the weather was uncommonly fine and the sun was very hot.
sentences.zh: 因此《海姆斯克林格》记载，天气异常晴朗，阳光非常炽热。

sentences.en: So the men laid aside their armour and went ashore only with their shields, helmets, spears and swords.
sentences.zh: 所以士兵们卸下了盔甲，只带着盾牌、头盔、长矛和剑上了岸。

sentences.en: And many had also bows and arrows and they were all very merry.
sentences.zh: 许多人还带着弓箭，他们都非常高兴。

sentences.en: So heading off without your armour, what could possibly go wrong?
sentences.zh: 所以不穿盔甲就出发，究竟能出什么岔子呢？

sentences.en: So Tosti, we're told in the sagas, says, what are we doing?
sentences.zh: 萨迦传奇告诉我们，托斯蒂说，我们在干什么？

sentences.en: Let's take the armour with us.
sentences.zh: 把盔甲也带上吧。

sentences.en: It's mad to leave our armour behind in enemy territory.
sentences.zh: 在敌方领土上把盔甲落在后面太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I fear you've lost your wits.
sentences.zh: 我怕你是脑子坏了。

sentences.en: So his people skills kicking in again there.
sentences.zh: 所以他的情商又一次发挥了作用。

sentences.en: We are told that everybody hates Tosti so much that, quote, nobody would listen to him.
sentences.zh: 据说每个人都极其讨厌托斯蒂，以至于“没有人肯听他的”。

sentences.en: I love that detail.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个细节。

sentences.en: Now the thing is, Tosti, of course, at this point is redundant.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，当然了，此时的托斯蒂已经是多余的了。

sentences.en: Really, there's no point in Tosti anymore.
sentences.zh: 说实话，托斯蒂已经没有什么存在的意义了。

sentences.en: But you might say, worse than redundant, that he's an active problem because everyone in York hates him.
sentences.zh: 但你可能会说，比多余更糟的是，他成了一个实质性的问题，因为约克的每个人都恨他。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it doesn't surprise me that nobody listens to him.
sentences.zh: 所以没有人听他的，我一点也不觉得奇怪。

sentences.en: I mean, at this point, if you're Harold Haldradi, you're probably thinking, well, I'm going to get rid of this bloke pretty soon because I don't need him anymore.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，此时此刻，如果你是哈罗德·哈德拉达，你可能会想，好吧，我很快就要摆脱这家伙了，因为我不再需要他了。

sentences.en: Do they leave their armour behind?
sentences.zh: 他们真的把盔甲留下了吗？

sentences.en: There are some people who think they wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为他们不会这么做。

sentences.en: So there's a guy called Tom Shippey, great scholar of Norse literature, great Tolkien scholar, who says in his book, Laughing Shall I Die?
sentences.zh: 所以有一个叫汤姆·希皮的人，北欧文学的伟大学者，伟大的托尔金学者，他在他的书《笑著我将死去？》中说：

sentences.en: He says, it's just not plausible that Harold Haldradi would have left his armour behind.
sentences.zh: 他说，哈罗德·哈德拉达会把盔甲落在后面，这根本不合常理。

sentences.en: This feels like a detail invented by saga writers to excuse his defeat.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是萨迦传奇的作者们为了掩饰他的失败而编造的一个细节。

sentences.en: It's basically like saying you wore the wrong boots in a football match that you were expected to win.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就像是在一场你本该赢下的足球比赛中说你穿错了靴子一样。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Let's assume they did leave their armour behind because the sagas are so, they emphasise it again and again.
sentences.zh: 让我们假设他们确实把盔甲留下了，因为那些传奇故事实在是太强调这一点了，一次又一次地提及。

sentences.en: They set off towards Stamford Bridge.
sentences.zh: 他们向斯坦福桥进发。

sentences.en: Now this is 15 miles away.
sentences.zh: 现在这里距离有15英里远。

sentences.en: Some of them would have had horses.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人会有马。

sentences.en: Most of them wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 大多数人没有。

sentences.en: So they're proceeding probably at walking pace on what we're told is a hot day.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能正以步行的速度前进，据我们所知，那天天气很热。

sentences.en: Don Holway in his book, The Last Viking, about Harold Haldradi estimates that this would have taken them probably five hours or so.
sentences.zh: 唐·霍尔韦在他关于哈罗德·哈德拉达的书《最后的维京人》中估计，这可能花了他们大约五个小时左右。

sentences.en: So in other words, they probably get to Stamford Bridge when the sun's at its height around midday.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们大概在太阳当空的中午时分到达了斯坦福桥。

sentences.en: We've already heard they were very merry.
sentences.zh: 我们已经听说他们非常高兴。

sentences.en: Of course, they're in good form.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们状态很好。

sentences.en: They've beaten the only army in the north of England.
sentences.zh: 他们击败了英格兰北部的唯一一支军队。

sentences.en: There's no real threat to them.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说没有什么真正的威胁。

sentences.en: They've had a great night of feasting.
sentences.zh: 他们度过了饮酒作乐的美妙一夜。

sentences.en: And we know that they haven't sent out any scouts or patrols because they don't really need to.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们没有派出任何侦察兵或巡逻队，因为他们根本不需要。

sentences.en: Now we're told they get to this bridge across the River Derwent.
sentences.zh: 现在据说他们到达了跨越德温特河的这座桥。

sentences.en: It's a wooden bridge going kind of east to weSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一座大致呈东西走向的木桥。

sentences.en: Kind of rough, rough boards across.
sentences.zh: 大概铺着粗糙的木板。

sentences.en: With gaps in.
sentences.zh: 中间有缝隙。

sentences.en: With gaps, yeah.
sentences.zh: 有缝隙，是的。

sentences.en: Through which you could stick a sword or spear, in fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你可以通过这些缝隙刺入剑或长矛。

sentences.en: Potentially, if required.
sentences.zh: 如果需要的话，潜在地可以。

sentences.en: So they cross the bridge from the southeastern side to the northwestern side.
sentences.zh: 所以他们从东南侧过桥走到西北侧。

sentences.en: And now we're told in the sagas comes the key moment as they see a kind of dust cloud on the western horizon coming from the direction of York.
sentences.zh: 现在萨迦传奇告诉我们，关键时刻来了，他们看到西方地平线上升起了一团尘土，来自约克方向。

sentences.en: And Harold Haldradi says to Tostig, what is this, horseman?
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·哈德拉达对托斯蒂说，这是什么，骑兵吗？

sentences.en: And Tostig said, oh, well, this must obviously be the group bringing the hostages.
sentences.zh: 托斯蒂说，哦，好吧，这显然一定是带来人质的队伍。

sentences.en: Or maybe it's a party of kind of bigwigs from York who've come to pay you, you know, homage to bend the knee, as it were.
sentences.zh: 或者也许是一群来自约克的权贵，他们来向你致敬，可以说是来臣服的。

sentences.en: And then the wonderful bit from Snorri, the nearer this force came, the greater it appeared, and their shining arms glittered like a field of broken ice.
sentences.zh: 然后是斯诺里写下的精彩片段，这支军队越近，就显得越庞大，他们闪闪发光的武器像一片破碎的冰面一样闪耀。

sentences.en: Wonderful description, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 精彩的描述，不是吗？

sentences.en: And you get this sense in the sagas of Harold Haldradi watching this force appear and the light glittering on the tips of the spears.
sentences.zh: 你在萨迦传奇中能感受到这种感觉：哈罗德·哈德拉达看着这支军队出现，阳光在长矛尖端闪烁。

sentences.en: And this dreadful sinking feeling when he realises, I've made a really dreadful mistake here, because these are not the hostages.
sentences.zh: 还有那种可怕的下沉感，当他意识到，我在这里犯了一个极其可怕的错误，因为这些根本不是人质。

sentences.en: This is an army.
sentences.zh: 这是一支军队。

sentences.en: This is really one of the most dramatic, breathtaking, unexpected moments in all English history, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我想说，这真的是整个英国历史上最戏剧性、最惊心动魄、最意想不到的时刻之一。

sentences.en: And one of the most iconic exchanges in all of English history.
sentences.zh: 也是英国历史上最具标志性的对话之一。

sentences.en: So who is this?
sentences.zh: 那么这是谁呢？

sentences.en: It is, of course, Harold Godwinson, who's been waiting on the south coast all summer to face the Normans.
sentences.zh: 当然是哈罗德·戈德温森，他整个夏天都在南海岸等待迎战诺曼人。

sentences.en: Now, there are two versions of what has happened here.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于这里发生的事情有两种说法。

sentences.en: Here's the one that is the one that you learn as a child in school, and it's the really exciting one.
sentences.zh: 这就是你在学校里作为孩子学到的那种版本，而且是非常激动人心的那个版本。

sentences.en: Remember, Harold Godwinson released his men to bring in the harvest on the 8th of September and went back to London.
sentences.zh: 记住，哈罗德·戈德温森在9月8日放他的手下去收割庄稼，然后回到了伦敦。

sentences.en: In this sort of legendary version of the story, he hears on the 19th that Hardrada and Tostig have landed in the north.
sentences.zh: 在这个传说版本的的故事中，他在19日听说哈德拉达和托斯蒂在北方登陆了。

sentences.en: He immediately musters his men, what men he can, and then he starts riding out of London, gathering men as he passes.
sentences.zh: 他立即召集他的手下，能召集多少就召集多少，然后开始骑马离开伦敦，一路上不断集结人那。

sentences.en: So that would be on the day of the Battle of Fulfur, the 20th of September.
sentences.zh: 所以那将是在富尔福德战役当天，即9月20日。

sentences.en: Now, normally, that journey to York would take two weeks.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，去约克的旅程需要两周时间。

sentences.en: And in the kind of legendary version of the story, somehow pushing his men beyond the limits of endurance, he does it in four and a half days.
sentences.zh: 而在那种传奇般的故事版本中，他不知何故将手下的极限推到了超出耐力的地步，在四天半内就完成了。

sentences.en: And for historians who love Harold Godwinson, they say, come on, this bloke is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 对于热爱哈罗德·戈德温森的历史学家来说，他们会说，拜托，这家伙太厉害了。

sentences.en: He's a brilliant general.
sentences.zh: 他是个杰出的将军。

sentences.en: He's a great organiser.
sentences.zh: 他是个伟大的组织者。

sentences.en: And what an inspirational Churchillian figure he must be to push his men to cover such a distance in so short a time.
sentences.zh: 他一定是一个鼓舞人心的丘吉尔式人物，能够促使手下在如此短的时间内走完这样的距离。

sentences.en: But the trend among more modern historians, more recent historians, is to say, come on, if it takes you two weeks, you're not going to do it in four days.
sentences.zh: 但现代历史学家、更近期的历史学家的趋势是说，得了吧，如果你需要两周时间，你是不可能在四天内完成的。

sentences.en: That's just not plausible.
sentences.zh: 这根本不合常理。

sentences.en: But I think they can be discounted.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它们可以被忽略。

sentences.en: You think so?
sentences.zh: 你也这么认为吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The cynic's explanation is that actually Harold Godwinson left much earlier, that probably he had words that Hadrard had first entered the Humber,
sentences.zh: 愤世嫉俗者的解释是，哈罗德·戈德温森其实出发得早得多，可能在哈德拉达刚进入亨伯河时，他就已经得到了消息，

sentences.en: and then he started mestering his men.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始集结手下的军队。

sentences.en: And probably it did take them about two weeks.
sentences.zh: 而且这大概确实花了他大约两周时间。

sentences.en: So maybe they're not quite as exhausted.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他们并没有那么筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: But also, bear in mind, you know, we were talking in the last episode about the incredible military apparatus that an English king can command.
sentences.zh: 但也要记住，你知道的，我们在上一集里讨论过英国国王能够调动的惊人军事力量。

sentences.en: He can command people from the north.
sentences.zh: 他可以调动来自北方的人马。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: You know, there are deep reserves of manpower.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那里有深厚的人力储备。

sentences.en: They haven't all been wiped out at Fulford.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有在福尔福德之战中全部被消灭。

sentences.en: So, you know, I assume he could do what seems to have happened in the wake of Stamford Bridge, which is he has a cavalry force.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我推测他能做到似乎在斯坦福桥之战后发生的事情，那就是他拥有一支骑兵部队。

sentences.en: And as he goes, he raises men who then accompany him.
sentences.zh: 而且在行军途中，他不断召集随后随行的人员。

sentences.en: That's quite possible, too.
sentences.zh: 这也是完全可能的。

sentences.en: That is absolutely possible.
sentences.zh: 那是绝对可能的。

sentences.en: Either way, by the evening of the 24th of September, so the previous evening to the day that he meets Hadrard, by that evening, he has reached the village of Tadcaster,
sentences.zh: 无论如何，到9月24日傍晚，也就是他遭遇哈德拉达的前一天傍晚，在那天傍晚，他已经抵达了塔德卡斯特村，

sentences.en: which is 10 miles southwest of York.
sentences.zh: 该村位于约克郡西南部10英里处。

sentences.en: Having covered a distance of almost 200 miles.
sentences.zh: 此时他已行进了将近200英里的距离。

sentences.en: He will undoubtedly, by this point, have heard about Edwin and Mork are being defeated.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，他无疑已经听说了埃德温和莫克尔战败的消息。

sentences.en: He will have heard that York has surrendered.
sentences.zh: 他一定听说约克已经投降了。

sentences.en: And what he does is he waits.
sentences.zh: 而他所做的就是等待。

sentences.en: He allows Hadrard to have his feast, to feast at the ships.
sentences.zh: 他任由哈德拉达去享用他的宴席，在船上大快朵颐。

sentences.en: He keeps a low profile.
sentences.zh: 他保持低调。

sentences.en: Then when door breaks, while Hadrard is off walking through the countryside with no armor, Harold Godwinson marches into York, but doesn't stop there,
sentences.zh: 接着在天亮时分，当哈德拉达赤手空拳、毫无防备地在乡间漫步时，哈罗德·戈德温森长驱直入进入约克，但并没有停下脚步，

sentences.en: which you might expect him to do.
sentences.zh: 而这本来可能是你预料他会做的。

sentences.en: He keeps going.
sentences.zh: 他继续前进。

sentences.en: He obviously is told Hadrard is going to Stamford Bridge to get the supplies and the hostages.
sentences.zh: 他显然得到了消息，得知哈德拉达正前往斯坦福桥获取补给和人质。

sentences.en: And Godwinson says, right, I'm going there, too, and we will intercept him there.
sentences.zh: 于是戈德温森说，好，我也要去那里，我们要去那里拦截他。

sentences.en: It's a bold call.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大胆的决定。

sentences.en: He's going to risk it all on one battle.
sentences.zh: 他打算把一切都押在一场战斗上。

sentences.en: I mean, this is what people keep doing in this story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是人们在这个故事里一直不断在做的事，不是吗？

sentences.en: So this is what Hadrard sees coming in the distance.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是哈德拉达在远处看到的情景。

sentences.en: Harold Godwinson with the English army, and they're flying Godwinson's war banner, which is a red flag embroidered with a white fighting man.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·戈德温森率领着英国军队，他们正举着戈德温森的战旗，那是一面绣着一个白色战斗勇士的红旗。

sentences.en: Yeah, the fighting man of Wessex.
sentences.zh: 是的，威塞克斯的战斗勇士。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So Hadrard thinks, oh, no.
sentences.zh: 所以哈德拉达心想，哦，不。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Because the Englishmen have more men.
sentences.zh: 因为英国人有更多的人马。

sentences.en: They have 12,000 men.
sentences.zh: 他们有12,000名士兵。

sentences.en: He perhaps has 8,000.
sentences.zh: 而他大概只有8,000人。

sentences.en: And if we can believe the sagas, his men have, by and large, left their armor behind.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能相信那些萨迦史诗的话，他的手下基本上都把盔甲留在后方了。

sentences.en: So what's Hadrard to do now?
sentences.zh: 那哈德拉达现在该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: Now we're dependent completely on the sagas, really.
sentences.zh: 现在我们真的完全要依赖萨迦史诗了。

sentences.en: The sagas say he sent three men.
sentences.zh: 萨迦史诗记载他派出了三个人。

sentences.en: He said, bring my three fastest riders and sent them back to Rickle for help.
sentences.zh: 他说，把我的三个最快骑手带来，并派他们星夜赶回里克尔寻求援助。

sentences.en: Get the rest of the men.
sentences.zh: 把剩下的人都叫来。

sentences.en: But if he did that, he must have known that that would take, even if they're riding really faSt.
sentences.zh: 但如果他真的这么做了，他一定知道那会需要时间，哪怕他们骑得非常快。

sentences.en: And then they basically move really quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且他们基本上会以极快的速度行动。

sentences.en: It will take three, four hours for them to get to him.
sentences.zh: 他们赶到他那里也需要三到四个小时。

sentences.en: The key would be to find a bridge, say, and hold the bridge.
sentences.zh: 关键在于找到一座桥，比方说，并坚守住这座桥。

sentences.en: If only there were a bridge that he could hold out at.
sentences.zh: 要是有那么一座桥能让他据守就好了。

sentences.en: And he says to his captains, the Englishmen shall have a hard fray of it before we give ourselves up for loSt.
sentences.zh: 他对他的指挥官们说，在我们向绝境投降之前，英国人将免不了要经历一场苦战。

sentences.en: No question about that.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So now there are two great incidents that feel that they're very J.R.R.
sentences.zh: 所以现在发生了两个重大事件，感觉非常像是J·R·R·

sentences.en: Tolkien or the stories of King Arthur, or indeed the Norse myths.
sentences.zh: 托尔金的作品、亚瑟王的故事，或者干脆就是北欧神话。

sentences.en: First of all, he wheels his horse to bring up his army.
sentences.zh: 首先，他调转马头来集结军队。

sentences.en: And he says, bring forth the land waster, the raven banner.
sentences.zh: 他说，把土地毁灭者、渡鸦战旗拿出来。

sentences.en: And at that point, his horse stumbles and throws him to the ground in front of his men, which is a terrible omen.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，他的马绊了一下，把他摔倒在他士兵面前的地上，这是个可怕的征兆。

sentences.en: But he is quick-witted, as we know.
sentences.zh: 但他反应机敏，正如我们所知。

sentences.en: And he says, ha, ha, ha, a fall is good fortune.
sentences.zh: 他说，哈哈，跌倒是个好兆头。

sentences.en: And Dominic, that is something that will also be told of William landing at Pevensey.
