sentences.en: Whistling of arrows.
sentences.zh: 箭矢的呼啸声。

sentences.en: Yeah, all of that.
sentences.zh: 对，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So let's go with the sagas.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还是根据萨迦的记载来吧。

sentences.en: Which are the, yeah, and try to, I'm just going to try to have some fun with the sagas and see what we think could have happened.
sentences.zh: 也就是，对，我只是打算试着从萨迦中找点乐子，看看我们认为可能发生过什么。

sentences.en: Hardrada wants to hold off the English for as long as possible before, let's say, 4,000 men arrive from Rickle.
sentences.zh: 哈拉尔德想要尽可能长时间地拖住英国人，比方说，直到4000人从里克尔赶到之前。

sentences.en: They'll take four hours, so he's got a long time to fight.
sentences.zh: 他们需要四个小时，所以他有很多时间来战斗。

sentences.en: But, as you said, that bridge is going to come in very useful.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如你所说，那座桥将派上大用场。

sentences.en: So it's a narrow wooden footbridge, we're told.
sentences.zh: 所以据我们所知，那是一座狭窄的木制人行桥。

sentences.en: We're also told, the banks of the river are too steep and the water is too deep to cross anywhere but the bridge.
sentences.zh: 我们还被告知，河岸太陡，水太深，除了桥之外哪里都过不去。

sentences.en: If you're on the other side, the English have to, they can only use the footbridge to cross.
sentences.zh: 如果你在另一边，英国人必须，他们只能通过人行桥过河。

sentences.en: So he puts most of his men, the sagas say, on the far sort of southeastern bank.
sentences.zh: 所以萨迦说，他把大部分人部署在遥远的东南岸一带。

sentences.en: And then he orders his elite, his vanguard, his houseguards, his trained professional soldiers to form a shield wall at the far end of the bridge, the western bank.
sentences.zh: 然后他命令他的精锐、他的先锋、他的近卫军、他训练有素的职业士兵在桥的另一端——西岸——组成一面盾墙。

sentences.en: And basically, if they can hold the bridge, they will be all right.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果他们能守住这座桥，他们就会安然无恙。

sentences.en: And then, say the sagas, there is this long struggle.
sentences.zh: 然后，萨迦说，这是一场漫长的拉锯战。

sentences.en: The English are firing arrows at them, throwing spears at them, basically trying to dislodge this shield wall from the narrow footbridge.
sentences.zh: 英国人向他们发射箭矢，投掷长矛，基本上是试图将这道盾墙从狭窄的人行桥上驱逐出去。

sentences.en: Because once they've got the bridge, they can then pour across and attack the rest of the Norwegians.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦他们拿下了桥，他们就可以蜂拥过桥，攻击其余的挪威人。

sentences.en: And in the English sources that we have, later chronicles, let's say 100 years later, some of them, they tell the story.
sentences.zh: 而在我们拥有的英国史料中，后来的编年史，比方说晚了100年的某些史料，它们讲述了这个故事。

sentences.en: Again, it does feel a little bit like a well-known formula that one by one,
sentences.zh: 同样，这确实感觉有点像一个众所周知的套路，一个接一个，

sentences.en: the Norsemen are whittled down until there is just one anonymous Norseman holding the bridge alone against the English.
sentences.zh: 挪威人被不断消灭，直到只剩下一个匿名的挪威人独自在桥上对抗英国人。

sentences.en: So, this is Henry of Huntingdon.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是亨廷顿的亨利。

sentences.en: He was born in about 1088.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1088年左右。

sentences.en: So, he's born about 20 years after the battle.
sentences.zh: 所以他大约出生于战役后20年。

sentences.en: Might he have heard eyewitness accounts?
sentences.zh: 他可能会听到目击者的叙述吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难说。

sentences.en: But anyway, this is what he says.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，他是这么说的。

sentences.en: A single Norwegian, whose name should have been remembered, posted himself on the bridge.
sentences.zh: 一个本该被人们记住名字的孤身挪威人，驻守在桥上。

sentences.en: And chopping down more than 40 English with a battle axe, his country's weapon, halted the advance of the whole English army.
sentences.zh: 他用战斧——他国家的武器——砍倒了40多名英国人，阻挡了整个英国军队的推进。

sentences.en: And this is William of Malmesbury.
sentences.zh: 而这是马姆斯伯里的威廉。

sentences.en: And you said, Tom, I think that he's about the same generation, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 你说过，汤姆，我认为他大约是同一代人，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, he might, again, just have heard eyewitness accounts.
sentences.zh: 所以，他可能也只是听到了目击者的叙述。

sentences.en: I mean, William of Malmesbury is a very great historian, probably the greatest English historian since Bede.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，马姆斯伯里的威廉是一位非常伟大的历史学家，可能是自比德以来最伟大的英国历史学家。

sentences.en: So, not to be discounted altogether.
sentences.zh: 所以不能完全不把他的话当回事。

sentences.en: Well, let us believe him.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们相信他吧。

sentences.en: He says, given the chance to surrender and being assured that a man of such bravery could expect the greatest mercy from the English,
sentences.zh: 他说，在获得投降的机会并被保证拥有如此勇敢的人可以从英国人那里获得最大的宽大处理后，

sentences.en: he, this is this lone Norseman, ridiculed those who tried to bargain with him.
sentences.zh: 他——也就是这个孤身一人的挪威人——嘲笑了那些试图与他讲条件的人。

sentences.en: And scorned the cowards who were unable to overcome one man.
sentences.zh: 并鄙视那些无法战胜一个人的懦夫。

sentences.en: And then, this very memorable moment, one Englishman gets under the bridge.
sentences.zh: 然后，在这个非常难忘的时刻，一个英国人潜到了桥下。

sentences.en: Some accounts say he's sort of made a makeshift boat for himself and is kind of floating under the bridge.
sentences.zh: 有些记载说他为自己做了一个简易小船，正漂在桥底下。

sentences.en: And then he stabs his sword up through the planks of the bridge.
sentences.zh: 然后他把剑从桥木板的缝隙向上刺去。

sentences.en: The gap between the boards that we mentioned before.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们前面提到的木板之间的缝隙。

sentences.en: The gap between the boards into the Norseman's...
sentences.zh: 通过木板间的缝隙刺入挪威人的……

sentences.en: Nether parts.
sentences.zh: 下半身。

sentences.en: Nether regions, exactly.
sentences.zh: 下体，没错。

sentences.en: The Norseman falls.
sentences.zh: 挪威人倒下了。

sentences.en: A great cheer erupts from the English army.
sentences.zh: 英国军队爆发出一阵巨大的欢呼声。

sentences.en: And then, like, kind of the orcs at the end of the Fellowship of the Ring, they pour across the bridge.
sentences.zh: 然后，就像《指环王》结尾的半兽人一样，他们蜂拥过桥。

sentences.en: Dominic, you're not comparing the English to the orcs.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你可别把英国人比作半兽人。

sentences.en: Yeah, but Tom, I don't actually think that.
sentences.zh: 对，但汤姆，我其实不是那个意思。

sentences.en: This is what a great historian does with his imagination.
sentences.zh: 这就是伟大的历史学家运用想象力的方式。

sentences.en: I'm seeing it from the Norwegian perspective.
sentences.zh: 我是从挪威人的视角来看待的。

sentences.en: I just want to pay tribute here to my very first history teacher, Major Morris.
sentences.zh: 我只想在这里向我的第一位历史老师莫里斯少校致敬。

sentences.en: He would narrate our stories, very like you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 他会给我们讲故事，非常像你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: But he was also a brilliant artiSt.
sentences.zh: 但他也是一位才华横溢的艺术家。

sentences.en: And he drew a picture of this sole Norseman standing on the bridge, smiting the English.
sentences.zh: 他画了一幅这个孤身挪威人站在桥上痛击英国人的画。

sentences.en: And then he did one of the Englishmen in the boat, gliding up to the bridge.
sentences.zh: 然后他又画了一个英国人在船里悄悄滑向桥下的情景。

sentences.en: And then he had an excellent drawing of the spear being shoved up through the gap.
sentences.zh: 接着他有一幅极佳的画作，描绘了长矛从缝隙中刺上来的场景。

sentences.en: Oh, no way.
sentences.zh: 噢，不会吧。

sentences.en: And the Norseman, arms and legs going out.
sentences.zh: 而那个挪威人，手脚大张。

sentences.en: And I must have been, I don't know, eight, nine when I saw that.
sentences.zh: 我当时一定，我不知道，八、九岁吧，当我看到那个的时候。

sentences.en: And I've never forgotten it.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会忘记它。

sentences.en: I can't compete with that because actually my art teacher, when I was that age, said I was the single worst person she'd ever taught in her 40-year career.
sentences.zh: 我没法与之相比，因为实际上我的美术老师在我那个年纪时说，我是她40年教学生涯中教过的最糟糕的人。

sentences.en: Mrs. Salt.
sentences.zh: 索尔特太太。

sentences.en: That was her verdict.
sentences.zh: 那是她的结论。

sentences.en: So I can't compete with Major Morris, I'm afraid.
sentences.zh: 所以恐怕我没法和莫里斯少校相比。

sentences.en: So what happens next?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: The English have piled across the bridge.
sentences.zh: 英国人已经成群结队地冲过了桥。

sentences.en: What can we tell from the sagas?
sentences.zh: 我们能从萨迦中看出什么？

sentences.en: What probably happened?
sentences.zh: 可能发生了什么？

sentences.en: And almost certainly the Norwegians would have formed a shield wall, a defensive shield wall and tried to hold out.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定，挪威人会组成一个盾墙，一个防御性的盾墙并试图死守。

sentences.en: And we can assume that effectively the English surrounded them again.
sentences.zh: 我们可以假设，实际上英国人再次包围了他们。

sentences.en: And then Dominic has a great historian kind of entered into the mind of Harold.
sentences.zh: 然后多米尼克展现出伟大的历史学家那种进入哈拉尔德内心世界的能力。

sentences.en: And if he has, shall I read what this great historian, namely yourself, has written about it?
sentences.zh: 既然他做到了，我来读读这位伟大的历史学家——也就是你自己——对此写了些什么，好吗？

sentences.en: So to explain, we're told in the sagas that Harold decides on one final charge without his helmet, without his armor.
sentences.zh: 为了解释清楚，萨迦中告诉我们，哈拉尔德决定进行最后一次冲锋，不戴头盔，不穿铠甲。

sentences.en: And again, yeah, it's the mark of a great historian, Tom, is their use of the imagination as well as the sources.
sentences.zh: 再次，对，一个伟大的历史学家的标志，汤姆，就是他们对想象力的运用以及对史料的使用。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So this is what you write in Adventures in Time.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你在《时间历险》中写的内容。

sentences.en: With two hands, he raised his huge steel ring sword and whispered one last prayer.
sentences.zh: 他双手举起巨大的精钢环柄剑，低声作了最后一次祈祷。

sentences.en: Then with a terrible roar of berserker fury, he hurled himself into the fray.
sentences.zh: 随后，伴随着狂战士般的滔天怒吼，他把自己掷入了激战之中。

sentences.en: And as he raged and slew, all his cares seemed to melt away.
sentences.zh: 当他狂怒厮杀时，他所有的烦恼似乎都消融了。

sentences.en: And he felt a lightness and joy he had not known for many years.
sentences.zh: 他感受到了一种多年未曾有过的轻松与快乐。

sentences.en: So that's you inhabiting the mind of a berserker warrior.
sentences.zh: 所以那就是你代入了狂战士的内心。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 难以置信。

sentences.en: But you know, it's method writing because I'm imagining my own mood before we do one of our Rest is History live shows on tour.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，这是体验派写作，因为我在想象我们进行巡回现场秀《历史的休息》之前的状态。

sentences.en: That is very much what you're like.
sentences.zh: 这确实很像你的状态。

sentences.en: You kind of froth at the mouth, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你有点口吐白沫，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, read the next bit and people will see exactly what I'm like before a show.
sentences.zh: 好吧，读读下一段，大家就会看到我在演出前到底是什么样的。

sentences.en: On he charged, his face a mask of dripping blood, a war cry on his lips, a battle song in his heart.
sentences.zh: 他继续冲锋，面部满是流淌的鲜血，嘴里喊着战吼，心中铭记着战歌。

sentences.en: He felt wonderfully happy.
sentences.zh: 他感到无比快乐。

sentences.en: He had never been happier.
sentences.zh: 他从未如此快乐过。

sentences.en: That's literally how I feel just before we go on stage to answer the listeners' questions.
sentences.zh: 这字面意思就是我上台回答听众提问之前的感受。

sentences.en: What's your favourite historical dinner party?
sentences.zh: 你最喜欢的历史晚宴是哪一个？

sentences.en: Who would win a fight between Jaco Macaco and Napoleon?
sentences.zh: 雅科·马卡科和拿破仑打架谁会赢？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly how I feel.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我完全是这种感觉。

sentences.en: So this is literally what happened to Harold Hardrada, to be clear.
sentences.zh: 所以说，哈罗德·哈德拉达遭遇的正是这种情况，明确一下。

sentences.en: In the sagas, he is killed either with an arrow or with a spear in the throat.
sentences.zh: 在传奇故事中，他是被一支箭或一支长矛刺穿喉咙而死的。

sentences.en: I think these details are very clearly taken from the Battle of Hastings.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些细节显然取材自黑斯廷斯战役。

sentences.en: But you know what, Tom?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: He deserves an ending like that.
sentences.zh: 他配得上这样的结局。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I think he died just like Boromir at Parth Garland at the end of the Fellowship of the
sentences.zh: 我觉得他的死法就像《魔戒》结尾处在帕斯吉兰德的

sentences.en: Ring.
sentences.zh: 博罗米尔一样。

sentences.en: So I think he is surrounded by English bodies.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得他的周围全是英格兰人的尸体。

sentences.en: He's in a pile of bodies.
sentences.zh: 他倒在尸堆之中。

sentences.en: He's peppered with arrows.
sentences.zh: 他身上插满了箭。

sentences.en: And obviously, all of this is the stuff that Tolkien is saturated in.
sentences.zh: 显然，这些全都是托尔金浸润其中的素材。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, it must be on Tolkien's mind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，托尔金心里一定在想这些。

sentences.en: As Tom Shippey would, I'm sure, absolutely agree.
sentences.zh: 正如汤姆·希佩一定也会绝对赞同的那样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: So Harold Hardrada falls and dies, let us hope, in this incredibly dramatic and worthy way.
sentences.zh: 所以哈罗德·哈德拉达倒下并死去了，但愿他是以这种极其戏剧化且悲壮的方式死去的。

sentences.en: Snorri Sturluson says, at this point, Harold Godwinson paused.
sentences.zh: 斯诺里·斯图鲁松说，就在这时，哈罗德·戈德温森停了下来。

sentences.en: And he said to the remaining Northmen and Tostig, who's still alive, we will give you peace and quarter if you surrender.
sentences.zh: 他对剩下的诺斯人以及依然活着的托斯蒂说，如果我们投降，我们会给你们和平与饶恕。

sentences.en: And again, Tostig behaves very gallantly.
sentences.zh: 而且托斯蒂再次表现得非常豪迈。

sentences.en: He says, no, I won't.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，我才不。

sentences.en: No, let's finish this.
sentences.zh: 不，让我们了结这一切吧。

sentences.en: Let's go to the end.
sentences.zh: 让我们战斗到最后一刻。

sentences.en: So there's a scowl called Arnor, who's quoted by the sagas.
sentences.zh: 因此有个叫阿尔诺的诗人在传奇故事中被引用。

sentences.en: The gallant men who saw him fall would take no quarter, him being Harold Hardrada.
sentences.zh: 那些看他倒下的豪杰们不接受饶恕，他就是哈罗德·哈德拉达。

sentences.en: One and all resolved to die with their loved king around his corpse in a corpse ring.
sentences.zh: 人人决心在尸环中与他们深爱的国王死在一起，死在他的尸体周围。

sentences.en: See, I think that's terrible.
sentences.zh: 你看，我觉得这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我觉得这太棒了。

sentences.en: I think that's, I actually almost started crying when I was reading that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这，我读到这里时甚至差点哭出来。

sentences.en: I was so moved.
sentences.zh: 我太感动了。

sentences.en: So by now, the Norwegian reinforcements are finally arriving, but it's far too late.
sentences.zh: 所以到这个时候，挪威的增援部队终于赶到了，但为时已晚。

sentences.en: Many of them are cut down too.
sentences.zh: 他们当中也有许多人被砍倒了。

sentences.en: And a few survivors, dozens, hundreds, it's hard to tell, do make it back to Rickall.
sentences.zh: 少数幸存者——几十人还是几百人，很难说——确实逃回了里卡尔。

sentences.en: They flee across the countryside.
sentences.zh: 他们逃过了乡间。

sentences.en: It was 24 ships go, and it was 300 ships that had arrived, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 出发时是24艘船，而到达时可是300艘船，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Harold Hardrada and Tostig's sons were not in the battle.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·哈德拉达和托斯蒂的儿子们没有参加这场战斗。

sentences.en: They'd stayed with the ships.
sentences.zh: 他们留在了船上。

sentences.en: And the next day, they rowed under flag of truce to York, where Harold Godwinson had installed himself victorious.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他们打着休战旗划向约克，哈罗德·戈德温森正以胜利者的姿态驻扎在那里。

sentences.en: And he was, as you would expect from Harold Godwinson, who's one of the greatest men who ever lived, he's very generous to them.
sentences.zh: 正如你对哈罗德·戈德温森的期望那样——他是历史上最伟大的人物之一——他对他们非常慷慨。

sentences.en: And he says, look, you know, it's a fair fight.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，你知道的，这是一场公平的战斗。

sentences.en: You know, all's fair in love and war.
sentences.zh: 你知道，情场如战场，兵不厌诈。

sentences.en: You can sail back to Norway as long as you don't do this again.
sentences.zh: 只要你们不再干这种事，就可以扬帆回挪威。

sentences.en: But he wants them to go.
sentences.zh: 但他希望他们离开。

sentences.en: And as you said, Tom, it takes them only 24 of their 300 ships to take the survivors back because so many have fallen.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，汤姆，他们300艘船现在只需要24艘就能把幸存者运回去，因为太多人阵亡了。

sentences.en: And Dominic, to the land of the Northmen came only a tale from far off, a rumour of the wrath and terror of Wessex.
sentences.zh: 而多米尼克，“传到诺斯人土地上的只有一个遥远的传说，一个关于威塞克斯之怒与恐怖的传闻。”

sentences.en: Oh, I love that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: Is that you?
sentences.zh: 这是你写的吗？

sentences.en: No, it's from Tolkien.
sentences.zh: 不，这是托尔金写的。

sentences.en: Oh, that's very good.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Well done, Tolkien.
sentences.zh: 托尔金干得漂亮。

sentences.en: It's the last sentence describing the Battle of Pelennor Fields.
sentences.zh: 这是描写珀兰诺平原战役的最后一句话。

sentences.en: And I have replaced Gondor with Wessex.
sentences.zh: 我把冈多替换成了威塞克斯。

sentences.en: Oh, that's very good.
sentences.zh: 哦，太妙了。

sentences.en: So that's one for you, one for Tabby and one for Tolkien fans everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以这个算你的，一个献给塔比，一个献给各地无数的托尔金书迷。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Well, Tabby, Tolkien fans and I are all delighted by that, I imagine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想塔比、托尔金的书迷和我对此都会感到很高兴的。

sentences.en: So this is the last gasp, Tom, of the Viking Age.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是维京时代的最后回光返照吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Or is it?
sentences.zh: 还是说并不是？

sentences.en: Well, is it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，真的是吗？

sentences.en: Is it, actually?
sentences.zh: 其实真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Because you could make two arguments here.
sentences.zh: 因为你可以提出两种论点。

sentences.en: One, you could say the Viking Age is already over because, of course, Christianity has already begun to transform Scandinavia.
sentences.zh: 第一，你可以说维京时代已经结束了，因为基督教当然已经开始改变斯堪的纳维亚。

sentences.en: We've had towns arriving in Scandinavia.
sentences.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚出现了城镇。

sentences.en: We've got kings.
sentences.zh: 我们有了国王。

sentences.en: The days of, you know, freebooting raiders are gone, actually.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种无拘无束四处劫掠的日子其实已经一去不复返了。

sentences.en: And Harold Hardrada, in many ways, is not a Viking.
sentences.zh: 而且哈罗德·哈德拉达在很多方面都算不上是一个维京人。

sentences.en: The other way you could say it is actually the Viking Age still has some time to run because there will be more Scandinavian attacks.
sentences.zh: 另一种说法是，其实维京时代还要延续一段时间，因为还会有更多来自斯堪的纳维亚的袭击。

sentences.en: Like, Svein, who sensibly turned down Tostig's offer, he does actually launch two raids after the Norman ConqueSt.
sentences.zh: 就像斯温，他明智地拒绝了托斯蒂的提议，在诺曼征服之后他确实发起了两次袭击。

sentences.en: And one of those has a very decisive impact on the course of William's reign, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将会看到的，其中一次对威廉统治的进程产生了决定性的影响。

sentences.en: It does, indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And, in fact, I was surprised when I looked this up.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我查阅资料时，我也感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: The last really serious attack, it was as late as 1152.
sentences.zh: 最后一次真正意义上的严重袭击，一直晚到1152年。

sentences.en: A guy called Einstein II, who was Harold Hardrada's great-great-grandson, raided the east coast of England.
sentences.zh: 一个叫埃斯泰因二世的人——他是哈罗德·哈德拉达的玄孙——袭击了英格兰东海岸。

sentences.en: So retro, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 真是太复古了，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, you're busy talking about the Crusades and things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你正忙着谈论十字军东征之类的事情。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, it's a Viking.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，居然是个维京人。

sentences.en: Come on, mate.
sentences.zh: 拜托，老兄。

sentences.en: It's the 12th century.
sentences.zh: 这可是12世纪啊。

sentences.en: But you can understand completely why people call Harold Hardrada the last Viking and why people always use this to end their kind of Viking survey books.
sentences.zh: 但你完全可以理解为什么人们把哈罗德·哈德拉达称为最后的维京人，为什么人们总是用他来为他们的维京通史类书籍收尾。

sentences.en: Because there is something about him, the mad adventures of his life, his travels, but also his sensibility.
sentences.zh: 因为他身上有一种特质，他那一生的疯狂冒险、他的游历，还有他的性格。

sentences.en: Composing all these poems in the face of danger, kind of laughing uncontrollably for no good reason.
sentences.zh: 在危险面前创作所有这些诗歌，莫名其妙地无法控制地大笑。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess I would just stick up for the Earls of Orkney, who do kind of hang around on the scene and continue to lead a Viking life,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我会为奥克尼伯爵们说句公道话，他们确实还在现场徘徊，继续过着维京人的生活，

sentences.en: composing poems and going on expeditions and things.
sentences.zh: 写写诗啊，进行探险什么的。

sentences.en: You've got to admit, Tom, they don't quite have the same cultural cachet as Harold Hardrada.
sentences.zh: 你得承认，汤姆，他们的文化吸引力确实不如哈罗德·哈德拉达。

sentences.en: No, they don't, but they are still around on the scene.
sentences.zh: 不，他们确实比不上，但他们仍然活跃在那个时代。

sentences.en: Tom Shippey has a lovely line where he's talking about the way he dies.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·希佩有一句很精彩的话，他在谈到哈罗德的死法时说。

sentences.en: And he says, even the way he dies at Stamford Bridge, this hubristic end where he's left his armor behind, or has he?
sentences.zh: 他说，甚至连他在斯坦福桥的死法，这种因为把盔甲留在后方而导致的狂妄自大的结局——或者他真的留下了吗？

sentences.en: Let's assume he's left his armor behind and he's surrounded by the English, but he fights onto the end.
sentences.zh: 让我们假设他真的把盔甲留在了后方，并被英格兰人包围，但他战斗到了最后一刻。

sentences.en: Tom Shippey says, this feels like the embodiment of the Viking spirit, arrogant, unlucky, self-possessed to the last, and accepting his fate with wry defiance.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·希佩说，这感觉就像是维京精神的化身，傲慢、倒霉、至死保持自我，并带着苦涩的挑衅坦然接受命运。

sentences.en: So that's the end of Harold Hardrada, but what of the victor?
sentences.zh: 这就是哈罗德·哈德拉达的结局，但胜利者又如何呢？

sentences.en: What of the man who's beaten him?
sentences.zh: 那个击败他的人怎么样了？

sentences.en: I think Harold Goldwinson has won an astounding victory.
sentences.zh: 我认为哈罗德·戈德温森取得了一场惊人的胜利。

sentences.en: It is one of the greatest victories at this point in the history of the English people.
sentences.zh: 这是英格兰民族历史上在这个阶段最伟大的胜利之一。

sentences.en: I mean, surely equivalent to any of the victories won by Alfred or Athelstan.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对堪比阿尔弗雷德或埃塞尔斯坦取得的任何一场胜利。

sentences.en: To have defeated a Norwegian army led by arguably the most famous warrior in Northern Europe, in all Europe, to have killed him, to have won such a crushing victory,
sentences.zh: 击败了一支由堪称北欧、乃至全欧洲最著名战士领导的挪威军队，杀死了他，取得了如此压倒性的胜利，

sentences.en: there is no chance the Norwegians will come back.
sentences.zh: 挪威人绝无卷土重来的可能。

sentences.en: I mean, Norway is out now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，挪威现在已经出局了。

sentences.en: It is a great tribute to the potency of Anglo-Saxon arMs.
sentences.zh: 这对盎格鲁-撒克逊武力的强大威力是一个极大的褒奖。

sentences.en: And to Harold Goldwinson's leadership, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这也是对哈罗德·戈德温森领导力的褒奖。

sentences.en: When you combine able leadership with the military resources of the Anglo-Saxon kingdom, Stamford Bridge is evidence that everything is fine, that it's ticking along.
sentences.zh: 当你把卓越的领导力与盎格鲁-撒克逊王国的军事资源结合起来时，斯坦福桥之战就证明了一切都很好，一切都在正常运转。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, Harold Goldwinson can feel very, very pleased with himself.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，哈罗德·戈德温森有充分的理由对自己感到非常非常满意。

sentences.en: For a few days, he remains in York to reSt.
sentences.zh: 他在约克停留了几天以作休整。

sentences.en: You can imagine his overwhelming relief.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象他那种如释重负的心情。

sentences.en: He's had months of waiting, months of uncertainty, and he knows now, for the time being, his kingdom is secure and his crown is safe.
sentences.zh: 他经历了数月的等待，数月的悬疑，现在他知道，至少目前他的王国稳固了，他的王位安全了。

sentences.en: And by now, it is well into the autumn and people just don't sail in, you know, with huge expeditions in this kind of, this time of year.
sentences.zh: 而且此时已是深秋，在这个季节里，人们根本不会带着庞大的远征军乘船入侵。

sentences.en: And then, at the turn of October, a messenger arrives in York.
sentences.zh: 然而就在十月之交，一个信使抵达了约克。

sentences.en: And when he's shown in to see Harold Goldwinson and he stammers out the words of the message, the blood drains from Harold's features.
sentences.zh: 当他被带去见哈罗德·戈德温森并结结巴巴地说出信件的内容时，哈罗德的面色瞬间煞白。

sentences.en: Because Tom, against all the odds, William of Normandy has landed at Pevensey.
sentences.zh: 因为汤姆，在所有人都意想不到的情况下，诺曼底的威廉在佩文西登陆了。

sentences.en: And now, for Harold and for the English, the road leads to Hastings and the final showdown.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于哈罗德和英格兰人来说，通往黑斯廷斯和最终决战的道路已经铺就。

sentences.en: Unbelievable tension.
sentences.zh: 难以置信的紧张感。

sentences.en: I mean, who would not want to hear that episode right now, to be honest?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说实话，谁现在不想听这一集呢？

sentences.en: And if you're a member of the Rest is History Club, the house culls of our podcasters, we like to think of them, you can.
sentences.zh: 如果你是“历史其余部分”俱乐部的成员——我们喜欢把他们看作我们播客的忠实核心——你就能听到。

sentences.en: And if you're not, then you can sign up at therestishistory.com and join us for slaughter at Senlac Hill.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是，那么你可以在therestishistory.com注册，加入我们，去森拉克山见证那场屠杀吧。

sentences.en: And all that thrilling bombshell, goodbye.
sentences.zh: 带着所有这些惊心动魄的重磅消息，再见。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
